By now, everyone knows that this is a bad game. It's not even available on the Steam Store as I write this. If you're reading this, you probably own it already.

So if it's bad, is it still fun? Kinda.

The story is *very* non-canon, with regular run-ins with Leon, Claire, Jill, and others, but they go on wild tangential adventures that are completely incongruous with Resident Evil 2 and 3. And what little story there is barely amounts to anything. It awkwardly wedges your team into scenarios already taking place in other games but doesn't add anything substantial to the lore. You're just a team of gun people on a mission to help or hurt Umbrella, depending on whether you're playing the main campaign or the DLC.

Speaking of which, the DLC is 7 chapters long and has as much content as the main campaign, placing you in the role of the good guys as opposed to the main game's Umbrella team. It's a little better put together, with a few objectives that reach beyond "kill and survive", and has more frequent set piece battles. It feels like it got just as much attention and budget as the main game, so it's worth playing if you want the full experience.

The gameplay is bad for a few pretty obvious reasons. It's sloppy as a shooter, it's even sloppier as a cover shooter, the AI is laughably terrible, and the presentation is decent but same-y throughout. One truly annoying feature is a waaaaay zoomed-in FOV, which actually made me nauseous until I got used to it. It's bad enough that I installed a mod (check the guides) to fix it, which was nice, but it made the game unstable and crash more frequently, which was not nice. YMMV.

It has a wild difficulty curve - on Veteran difficulty it had some punishing bottlenecks, and when I kicked the difficulty down to Normal to get through the DLC, my companions would still get regularly mowed down within seconds of an encounter beginning. Your health absolutely melts if you're being shot at by more than one enemy at a time, so if new enemies spawn and catch you unaware, it's a guaranteed restart until you learn those scripts. In terms of enemy design, it's a little strange and disappointing that soldiers are so much more dangerous than zombies, which make zombie-based areas even late in the campaigns feel much easier than soldier shoot-outs earlier on. Considering this is a game heavily influenced by Left 4 Dead, which made zombies VERY dangerous, this is a bummer.

So what about it is fun? It feels nice to be in the Resident Evil world, and I think the game does a decent job capturing a frenetic action style that keeps you engaged in combat even when dealing with the game's plethora of inconveniences. At its best, it can feel like a reasonable facsimile of Resident Evils 5, 6, and Revelations, in that weird horror-themed action rut the series found itself in during that middle era. There's nothing wrong with that style if you're willing to forget how much better the survival horror games before and after are. It can get your adrenaline going, and a few times when my team was fully dead in a tough firefight, I got through by the skin of my teeth in a way that felt very satisfying.

There's about a million better shooters and at least a dozen better Resident Evil games out there, but if you're a series completionist like I'm trying to be, you'll probably still have some fun with it. Just expect to feel equal parts frustration and bafflement at times when you realize this was a product that actually released, and also sold 2 million copies.

[h1]Resident Evil: Operation Absolute Garbage[/h1]

[i]Experience the Fear: Set in the terrifying world of Resident Evil.[/i]

[h2]Story[/h2]
The game is set in Raccoon City, during the events of Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. You play as a member of Unit Omega, a special U.S. Umbrella Security Service (U.S.S.) squad tasked with cleaning up the city and eliminating survivors to cover up Umbrella’s experiments. The story is told from the perspective of the “bad guys,” giving a unique view of events from the main series.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
Resident Evil: Operation Raccoon City is a squad-based third-person shooter. The game features 12 playable characters, six per team. On the Umbrella Security Service (USS) team: Vector (recon, cloaking), Lupo (leader), Beltway (explosives), Spectre (marksman), Bertha (medic), and Four Eyes (scientist, BOW programming). On the U.S. Special Ops team: Dee-Ay (leader), Willow (recon), Tweed (demolitions), Harley (medic), Shona (field scientist), and Party Girl (sniper).

Each character belongs to one of six classes—Assault, Recon, Surveillance, Field Scientist, Demolitions, or Medic—each with unique skills and abilities.

In addition to single-player, the game offers four-player co-op Raccoon Mode, where USS and U.S. Special Ops teams face off.

Heroes Mode is an online multiplayer mode where you play as Leon S. Kennedy, Claire Redfield, Jill Valentine, Carlos Oliveira, Ada Wong, HUNK, Nicholai Ginovaef, or the new character, Lone Wolf.

[h2]Enemies & Bosses[/h2]
Zombies in the game attack in different ways. If a zombie mutant gets too close, it will try to grab the player. To escape, you need to move the stick quickly. If you fail, your character gets temporarily infected. This gives small bonuses but slowly drains your health. If the infection isn’t stopped in time, your character loses control and attacks teammates until killed—but you can respawn afterward.

Other enemies you’ll face include Lickers, Hunters, and Cerberuses, but also stronger enemies and bosses like the Tyrant.

[h2]Environment[/h2]
The game takes place in Raccoon City during a viral outbreak. Unlike older Resident Evil games, it focuses less on solving puzzles and exploring, and more on fighting and taking cover. Most missions are straightforward, leading you from one goal to the next.

Levels often have multiple paths or side routes, especially in multiplayer, letting you move around strategically. Many areas are designed with cover in mind—walls, cars, barriers, and debris are placed to help players hide and plan attacks.

Some famous locations from Resident Evil 2 and 3 are included, such as: Raccoon City Police Department (RPD), downtown streets and alleyways, and underground sewers and labs

[h2]Visual Design & Sound Design[/h2]
The city is in total chaos. Streets are full of abandoned cars, rubble, and bodies. Fires burn, buildings crumble, and explosions happen everywhere, making it feel like the city has completely fallen apart.

In the background, you can hear distant sirens, collapsing buildings, and the moans of zombies echoing through alleyways. Some monsters, like Lickers or Nemesis, have unique sounds that warn you they’re nearby before you even see them.

[h2]Constructive Criticism[/h2]
You’re unable to reliably adjust the volume for sound effects, music, and dialogue. Technically, the settings exist—but the moment you exit the audio menu, they revert back. This is especially irritating when the blaring music becomes overwhelming and your only workaround is lowering the overall system volume in Windows.

Your AI teammates contribute very little and lack awareness, while enemies display lightning-fast reactions and pinpoint accuracy. Even on Casual difficulty, their damage output can feel unfair. The Lickers in particular are frustrating— their tongues have absurd reach, they can attack you through objects like ceiling grates, and the tongue sometimes snares you and triggers a repetitive and unclear QTE (like pressing C while moving the mouse from left to right) accompanied by a loud piano chord. The entire encounter design feels more bizarre than threatening. Enemies overall have a very stiff and ugly design.

The camera and controls feel awkward from the start, and the game provides no proper tutorial. You automatically snap into cover just by brushing against walls or objects, often when you don’t want to. Yet once you’re stuck against a wall, you can only peek from the right side—never the left—whether due to a bug or poor design, it’s hard to tell. With how many strange mechanics and issues the game has, both seem equally plausible.

Keybindings are another mess. The same button (E) is used for picking up items and lunging forward, leading to constant accidental actions. Weapon switching is mapped to the number 4 key for some reason—an awkward and unintuitive choice.

Even the weapons themselves lack satisfying feedback. Their sound effects are weak, and the lack of impact makes combat feel dull instead of thrilling.

At one point in the story, there’s even a scene where a zombie drives a truck in a deliberate attempt to run down Leon. It’s hard to take the situation seriously when the narrative leans into something that absurd.

Character models are noticeably rough, and the voice work doesn’t do much to improve their appeal. The performances often feel stilted or exaggerated, which breaks immersion rather than enhancing it.

The final battle and the ending fall flat as well—overly dramatic, poorly executed, and unintentionally cringe-worthy.

[h2]The Verdict[/h2]
Overall, the concept of playing as Umbrella security had potential and was an interesting take on the franchise. I played this game in May 2020, and honestly, I’m still not sure what else to say other than: I absolutely hated it. It’s not only the worst entry in the Resident Evil franchise in my experience—it may be the worst game I’ve ever played. I played this solo and have never tried multiplayer or co-op, but I can’t imagine it being any better. I could sit here forever and rant about this worthless game. It’s a buggy, frustrating, and sloppily designed mess where nothing works! Avoid at all costs!

[h2]Rating: 1/10[/h2]

I’ve been playing this game since I was a kid, and honestly ? I still love it.

It’s such a cool twist to explore Raccoon City from Umbrella’s perspective. Playing as a team of elite operatives cleaning up the mess they caused ? That alone is enough to make this game feel unique within the Resident Evil universe.

The characters are super stylish and memorable : Vector, Lupo, Four Eyes… they all have distinct personalities and gameplay styles. And the Spec Ops DLC ? Incredible. It flips the story on its head, and the Spec Ops team (shoutout to Party Girl, Willow, and the gang) are just as badass and fun to play as the U.S.S. crew.

I actually love that the game isn’t canon. It lets the devs go wild with the story, and it works. The WTF moments feel intentional and entertaining instead of lore-breaking. I mean, being able to choose whether or not to kill Leon at the end? That’s insane in the best way. It’s rare to have that kind of freedom in an RE game.

And let’s not forget : the cinematics and character design aesthetic, still gorgeous. The gritty, high-contrast look gives the game such a cool, dark, action-movie vibe that I wish more RE spin-offs had kept.

And honestly, it’s shameful that this game isn’t available for purchase anymore.
Yes, it had bugs. Yes, it was messy at times. But underneath that is a genuinely fun, ambitious, and unique RE experience that deserved better. With a few fixes and proper support, this game could’ve built a real cult following and it’s heartbreaking that new players can’t even try it unless they already own it. Capcom, bring it back. If you can get this game running past the weirdness that is the archaic and defunct Games for Windows Live, this game is a decent, maybe not great, Resident-Evil-flavored, Xbox-360-era action shooter where you go up against zombies, monsters, and the ever-annoying US military.

This game's main PvE gameplay loop is OVERALL pretty fun for an Xbox 360-era action shooter. However, upon replaying it for the first time to it's conclusion, at least for the main campaign, there are a few moments in the main story missions that take way longer due to some unfair frustrations.

Even on easy, just to have a casual romp through Raccoon City with overwhelming firepower, there are a few things that drag down the main missions, like any given section with a handful or more of the US military. One mission has you restarting generators, and each time you complete a section of that fight, a door opens up with about 12 military dudes who all focus fire, and you can go down in a fraction of a second. And the final mission has a huge fight between 12 or so soldier holding a wall an endless stream of zombies, of which half of them are the more powerful Crimson Head zombie variant. Get ready to die to a lot of unfair crap on that fight if you're playing solo.

The game really shines when it's just you fighting the monsters. With the right loadout, Hunters and Lickers aren't too tough, but there are sections where the game swarms you with Lickers and I can easily see those spots being a sour mark on the game's mixed record for some folks.

Another thing that lends to frustration is the controls. I played it on a controller, and the fact that the "A" button is responsible for dodge-leaping to the ground, picking up weapons, picking up ammo, picking up throwables and health items, and reviving teammates, means that, at least in hectic fights like the one before the main campaign final fight, I would be trying to revive a downed bot teammate, dodging past them, then swapping weapons off the ground 2-4 times before finally reviving them, and seemingly forever losing the weapon I chose on the pre-mission loadout screen unless I died and reset to checkpoint.

To me, the good outweighs the bad, but the bad in this game can be extremely frustrating, enough to probably keep me from wanting to replay this game again for a few years. What I wouldn't give for this game to get a remake or re-imagining with modern action shooter mechanics, and less of the 360-era wild-west of action shooter game development jank. Take what works for this game and mash it up with what's expected of modern action shooter controls and handling. And for goodness sake, either nerf or remove the US military. I'm here to shoot zombies, not dudes in body armor and wielding assault rifles.

It's currently March 30th, the game is currently delisted, but you can track the internal workings on SteamDB's website. The last major update was the game receiving a new internal build branch back in January of this year (2025). Presumably, Capcom is slowly working to remove the Games for Windows Live crap so they can relist, but with this game being the most mixed-to-disliked Resident Evil game, they probably aren't in any real hurry. As it stands, I can't play this game using my main Xbox account because its got modern account security features enabled, and the password is over 16 characters. So if you REALLY want to try this game, I would recommend making an alt account that you won't miss if anything happens to it due to lack of security options enabled.

We'll see how long it takes for this game to get relisted, or rather IF it does. But if you are ever in the mood for some action shooter in your Resident Evil, and this game is ever re-listed to buy, this might be the game for you. Though it would help if you had some nostalgia, or even tolerances, for Xbox-360-era games.

[h1]**As of 5/29/2023 this game still works. Crash fix stated below!**

This game came out a few months after Revelations in 2012.
It takes place before, during, and after the events of RE2 and most of RE3.

You play as one of the members of the Umbrella's Security Service division where you're tasked with destroying evidence and any involvement Umbrella had with the virus breakout being experienced.

The game/campaign is able to be played with a total of four friends, or solo with AI which is awesome!

For the longest time my game would crash on start up and never work. Which is the main reason Capcom made this game unable to purchase anymore. Because instead of removing the Games for Windows LIVE service that was discontinued, they just ignored it.

You can however get your game to work by doing these steps:

1) If you have Games for Windows LIVE installed already, go into Control Panel and uninstall both the Microsoft Games for Windows - LIVE Redistributable and MGFW Marketplace

2) Manually download and install the last/latest version of GFWL 3.9.95 (Check the guides for a download link)

3) Open the properties of "[i]RaccoonCity.exe[/i]", run it in Windows 7 Compatibility Mode and check the box Run as an Administrator.
(.exe located in Steam\steamapps\common\Resident Evil Operation Raccoon City\)

4) Start the game and either sign in to your old GWLF account or create a new one. Paste your CD key in, and wait about 5-10 minutes for it to complete. That's it!

It's a super fun game, if you like the series you'll enjoy it!

8/10[/h1]

Resident Evil: Operation Raccoon City is a game that tells the story from the operatives side from Umbrella when the outbreak happened and them doing damage control and cleanup. I basically summarized the whole campaign in one sentence and the silliest thing is we already knew all of this from previous games. So, why make this game? To shill and try to make some money from fans that enjoy the series while being the farthest from the rest of the franchise as possible. Now, I do understand that there are people that would want a squad based shooter like this and even in the Resident Evil universe, it is totally possible, but not on the budget and effort they put into it. So, if you do manage to get a fix to work for you, you are greeted with either playing the Campaign or online Multiplayer (yeah, good luck with that). There is 7 lengthy (30~ mins.) missions that go through the events I described previously. You can select from a few different characters which are unique classes with passive and active abilities to help for example, one is better at damage, one can carry 2 first aids, one cloaks. You are also able to play with up to 3 others if you find 3 other sorry souls to drag through this mess. So, AI it is which AI is about as basic as it gets, enemy and ally alike. teammates constantly stand in front of you or stand in the open and get shot rather than taking cover most of the time while not using abilities or picking up items or better guns. This wouldn't be as much of a problem if enemies weren't just bullet sponges and the fact that you can only carry 1 first aid spray because there is no inventory system like other RE titles. You get a primary, secondary, 1 first aid (unless you are medic), 1 antiviral (yeah, I will get to the "infection" mechanic), and 3 of each grenade. Since we are on the topic of weapons, all of them feel so weak with sometimes comical sounds. Don't get me wrong, guns to vary in damage, accuracy, fire rate, and a few other stats, but it all feels ridiculous when you have an anti-material rifle and have to shoot an unarmored soldier in the head TWICE with it then on the other hand, a heavy machine gun might take 10 - 15 bullets or sometimes 4 - 7.
Next, the enemies, and my god, I didn't expect to fight more soldiers than zombies in a Resident Evil game. These unnamed group of soldiers called Spec Ops and a few times called the Military (hint, they all look exactly the same) are more of a problem than the infected which the whole incident is about. The difference is they have guns and unless you are in cover (yes, this is a game where you sit in cover and shoot for 90% of it *bleugh*) they have near perfect accuracy and do more damage than you with basic and weaker guns. Now, the infected show up part of the time with little variety in enemies and there is no impact from them since they are mindless and the whole game is a shooting gallery. No resource management since stupidly placed, but definitely necessary infinite ammo boxes are placed all over the maps. Basic zombies just stumble around and might hit you, but not likely. Lickers return as the worst they have been as they take several magazines to kill and stupidly wonder on surfaces. Crimson heads even show up, but are just fast zombies, no burning needed. Unnamed parasites show up and take over zombies, mostly just run around and try to flank you. Besides that is the "bosses" so SPOILERS. First is Birkin, but it isn't a fight since you just run. Next is this guy named Nikolai which wants to foil your plans for some reason then just disappears like they ran out of funding or time, lol. Your fight is in at a church and he tries to snipe you while zombies attack you (like they work for him or something) which you just shoot him a million times then he just leaves, lol. Later, a fight with 3 Mr. X's which is silly because you just run around and unload all of your ammo, refill at the infinite ammo box and repeat until they die. Sensing a theme here? Very poor gameplay, dumb AI, lack of atmosphere with almost hallway like level design (yeah, the false sense of choice of direction is always blocked by "locked" doors and invisible walls), and a story that was written years ago which they managed to ♥♥♥♥ up. 
Even if you didn't play this excuse of a game, you already know what happens if you played the first RE titles. So, even if you didn't get the game for the story and campaign (you know, the main reason people play Resident Evil), the multiplayer is there. I don't know what it is like since no one plays it, but there is a few game modes that put players against each other. In closing, I am certain this is the worst Resident Evil I have played and I have played most of them now (Umbrella Chronicles might be worse, haven't played it). Even if you do play it, there isn't any takeaway, there isn't a good reason to take the time and play this entry. The game play, sound design, level design, story, characters, none of it feels fully developed and cohesive into an enjoyable and proper game in the franchise and I DO NOT recommend you "obtain it" and play it. I wouldn't play it again if I was payed to, it us just a waste of time.

The game itself can actually be a fun experience with others, and the DLC campaign where you play as US Special Forces takes what worked from the base campaign and focused in on that. This game has some jank in its trunk and I'm one of those folks who receives a mild euphoria from games with jank (Bloodlines, Alpha Protocol). No denying, getting it right out of the way right now the actual game has jankiness.

That's a good thing. See so many games today tend to be so over polished that they don't actually try anything new or provide the same experience a dozen other games already do. With jank usually comes some form of unique ideas or innovation, some miss the mark and others hit it dead on.

I think this one did it rather well. It's a squad based 3rd person shooter where the character you pick has some unique abilities and those are expanded upon by a point based unlocking system, so it encourages you to either replay through the story multiple times or be a part of the multiplayer. Not something we haven't seen before today but back in "the day" and for this series it was, it was something we didn't always see.

The story is RE2/3 reimagined. 

A What if, if you will of what if you were the bad guys. Now as we know bad guys in all forms of media are always cooler with the notable exception of Guts. They look cooler, they have that cooler weapon and somtimes they're even CALLED Cooler. We even have a playable Hunk fanboy for all the Hunkheads (trademarked, it's mine, MIIIIINE my precious) out there.

Remember in 2 when Mr. X is dropped in that cutscene and we see other containers we assume are other Mr. X's is. This game addresses it. How about what Mr. X, Birkin or the zombos when not chasing? Addressed. How about a situation where the events of the ending of RE2 didn't quite turn out the same way...also addressed, their is a choice. Though don't expect it to be game defining it was still a nice add in my book.

The gameplay has the bones of a run of the mill 3rd person game <at this time> and this is due, if I recall, to the developers being the folks who worked on those successful(?) SOCOM games. It has all the hallmarks of RE games such as herbs and healing sprays mixed with a Gears of War "revive me" hilarity. Guns feel different and of course there are some better than others but in my entire time playing through this game, on PC and PS3, never felt at a disadvantage.

So why do I have a bit of a fondness for this game especially looking back considering their seems to be a ton of things we see in nearly every game? That's because it reminds me of an old Commodore 64 game I used to play called G.I.Joe where you basically pick a character and fight another character on a small map where sometimes a 3rd party robot would appear that would attack you or the other person you fought against. 

See in this game, when you play the main story <as the Umbrella Security Service, would you like a G-virus with your fries?> you face off against the US military forces while a 3rd entity, the infected such as zombies and hunters, act as a more neutral faction. This means you could cause a special forces enemy to bleed out which would cause zombies and hunters to target them for you or in the case of my favorite character, throw a grenade that makes the special forces smell so wonderful the infected just have to get their number!

It's not a huge deal but this type of gimmick is something I enjoy and I'm always happy to see show up in a game as I don't think it's done enough. It makes it feel less like it's you against the game and more like you're experiencing an actual world.

The game works on a level stage like system where more or less you move from set piece to set piece but I found the levels to be large and expansive enough to not be boring. Added collectibles give you a bit more incentive to double, triple check places you have been to make sure you got everything before progressing only to find out you missed something because you're impatient < stop being impatient>.

Enemies are introduced in a manner where they introduce new mechanics, gimmicks or ideas as you progress into the later game where it's one of those "now take everything you've learned and excel".

Now, the graphics.

I wouldn't say they aged well because even at the time they weren't great but that adds some of that rough edged charm I find endearing. Birkin especially looks out of place compared to some of the other models. I'm not much of a graphics hound dog, I'll always be a champion of gameplay every time <look I still play Twisted Metal 1 and 2, Rogue trip and Critical Depth to this day. I just finished parasite Eve 1 again and played/beat parasite Eve 2 for the first time about a month ago>.

Not much else to say really about graphics.

GFWL aside (I was able to get it to work relatively easily), as a huge Resident Evil fan, I enjoy this game a lot. As an alternative way of experiencing the events from the second and third games, it's a fun "what if" take on the story.

When comparing this to some of the action-focused sequels, I enjoy this game more than RE6.

The auto-aiming pistol mechanic is unique, and there’s a large roster of classic RE enemies and locations.

Note: This game falls into the group of Capcom titles with predatory DLC pricing, similar to Dead Rising OTR (to this day, the DLC for that PC port does not work).

Playing around with a Samurai Edge while shooting Lickers, Hunters, Tyrants, Cerberus dogs, Crimson Heads, and more is incredibly enjoyable for a longtime fan.

This game also doesn’t harm the brand like RE6 or Umbrella Corps does.

I appreciate the controls and the variety of melee moves available. When it was populated, the versus modes—with a helicopter escape at the end, limited seats included—were really fun and compelling. I also like how you can use zombies to attack the gun-toting enemies in the game. There are plenty of clever nods to older titles and Easter eggs to be found.

It is what it is. Overall, it's a fun "what if" romp where you play as Umbrella bad guys instead of the series' heroes and cross paths with them a few times.

This game gets a lot of flack because it isn't like the other Resident Evil games. In terms of the series being a survival horror, this is NOT a good example of a Resident Evil game, but it is not a bad game. I actually thoroughly enjoy it a lot! It is a 3rd Person Shooter in the same world as the other Resident Evil games, but it does not play like a Resident Evil game. 

Do not go into this expecting a polished horror game. I get scared in the game because of overcrowding and getting my butt touched inappropriately by 20 Crimson Heads at once while Spec Ops troops chuck grenades at us. Especially in the last section, it gets overwhelming... But that's the fun of it. See, it's a very chaotic game, and I think it is a good example of what would have happened in the RE universe if it focused on Umbrella vs US Forces in the city; it would have been chaotic and hard to comprehend. I like to think this game would have been an awesome addition to the canonical lore if they didn't throw that away with them going after Leon and all.

Now, the game is a real cranky toddler and it doesn't like to start. You need an old version of Games for Windows Live to run it. It's worth giving it a look when it goes on sale, or if you have money to spare. They shouldn't be charging $30 dollars for this game since it's so old, unless they decide they are going to expand on this side of the RE Universe, which, I DEFINITELY think they should. I'll start this review with a humblebrag by saying that I beat the game's main campaign (Umbrella) on Professional difficulty. This was one of the most challenging experiences I've had in all my time playing Resident Evil. It also wasn't worth it.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2497119772

With that out of the way let's talk about the game. ORC is one of the more polarizing titles in the series. On release it was panned by series fans and got a lukewarm reception from professional critics. Game had balance and performance issues, PC port wasn't very good, the story contradicted existing lore and, in my opinion, worst of all of those things, is that game used (and still does) Games For Windows Live on PC. So how is it now?

Let's start with controls. I played the game with both Keyboard and Mouse combo and Gamepad and honestly the controls imo are fine for both. The only features I have issues with is the dodge move. To do it you need to sprint and then press the action button. This can be hard to do in a pinch and can also result in you diving instead of picking up an item you are running towards. However, good thing is that dodge move isn't mandatory, and the only enemies it's really useful against are Hunters and Tyrants. 

Visuals are a mixed bag. Player characters, both on Umbrella and US side are well done. Each character has a unique design that helps easily identify their role on the team and the quality of models themselves is also pretty good for the time. However, environments and some monster visuals and design can be questionable. For example, some zombies have oversized palms that look silly, and Licker limbs look like stuffed toys. Maybe it's just me, but when I look at them they remind me of cat paws. The human enemy models look fine for the most part, same with models of returning characters such as Leon and Jill. Claire imo looks somewhat bad but maybe it's just me. Game also has CG cutscenes that look very good even today.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ar-qKACbnkg

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IVd3hLBT7No

The music and overall sound is alright. I like the main theme that plays in the menu, and character voices are also distinct enough and fit their personalities, but overall sound is nothing special and music isn't all that memorable. It does the job and that's it.

On to the gameplay, the most questionable part of ORC. Let's start with the good. Do keep in mind that I played solo with AI bots so I'm just making an assumption here, but I'd imagine that if you can actually get 4 people to play together you can end up with very fun team based shooter. Each character has a unique role in the team and while there are 6 of them, you can only choose 4. Vector can go invisible to sneak behind enemies, mimic the enemy soldiers to walk up to them and avoid getting shot (though in my experience that doesn't always work, especially on higher difficulties. I'm not sure why). Beltway can place various types of mines on the battlefield that deal a lot of damage. Lupo is the main damage dealer of the party, being able to unlock a passive bodyarmor skill to tank enemy shots, reload weapons faster, and among her abilities are a buff that gives her incendiary ammo or infinite ammo for a few seconds. Bertha is the medic that can either buff her teammates or cure the T-Virus infection on demand. Her special melee execution also allows her to spawn green herbs on demand. Spectre is imo the most useless character, being able to more easily spot enemies and mark them for his team. Perhaps he's more useful in the PvP modes, but in the main campaign the only reason to pick him imo is if you just like the character himself. Finally, Four Eyes can manipulate the infected and B.O.W.s or even convert crimson heads to assist the team. Afaik there's no limit to how many she can control. The US Spec Ops characters have the exact same abilities. While in singleplayer the usefulness of many characters is limited due to the fact that your teammates don't often use abilities (I've never seen AI Beltway place mines, but I have seen Bertha spawn green herbs and Four Eyes convert zombies, so it clearly depends on the character), and in some situations on professional you're all but forced to pick a specific character to proceed (I'd love to see someone beat the final level on professional with someone other than Vector without dying), but I'd imagine with actual human players to assist the game could really shine. 

Your have a big arsenal of guns, from ARs and SMGs to LMGs, Sniper Rifles and even a rocket launcher. In addition to that, each character has melee attacks and two types of executions. One is generic and available to all characters, while the other is unique and utilizes a character's special ability. For example, if you have Mimicry equipped on Vector, after executing an enemy soldier he will mimic their looks. 

All of this sounds pretty fun so far. Big arsenal of guns, unique character roster that clearly emphasizes teamwork. So what could be wrong? First of all, most enemies in the game are huge bullet sponges. Even if you use the most powerful sniper rifle and get only headshots, enemy soldiers can take 3 shots to the head before dying. Zombies usually die in 2 shots to the head or so, but Hunters and Lickers are huge bullet sponges, able to take more than two mags from an assault rifle. Shotguns are much more useful, but they limit your range capabilities severely and on some maps can lead to you being pretty much useless to the team. The game also seems to have issues with hit detection and your weapons overall can feel pretty inaccurate at times. Another issue is enemy damage. Enemies KNOW that they are bullet sponges and they aren't afraid of abusing this. Enemy soldiers will rush your position and they will blast you in the face with the shotgun completely ignoring the fact that your 3 AI teammates are all firing at them. AI wants you dead and won't rest until you and your entire bloodline is erased from this planet. This can be downright immersion breaking at times. Another issue is the AI itself. Both enemies and friendlies can get stuck or start running back and forth in place. Thankfully you don't have to wait for NPCs to arrive and after you reach a checkpoint they get teleported to you, so it's not a huge issue, but it does happen and is annoying. Basically, main issues of ORC gameplay-wise are the sponginess of enemies and the overall lack of polish. 

Game also isn't very long. If you don't buy the DLC that includes the US campaign, you only get 7 missions which can be beaten in a single evening, especially on easier difficulty settings. While the game nowdays is pretty cheap (at least in my currency), it's still something to keep in mind. The story isn't anything special either. It's alright and has a few twists including two different endings for the Umbrella side, but overall it's just there as an excuse for you to visit locations from the original games. I think the biggest issue is that the game doesn't really start contradicting the original games until you meet Leon and Claire, so if developers didn't add that part, ORC could've easily been part of the canon. As it is, it's unlikely we'll ever see the members of the Wolfpack again, and it's pretty disappointing since they are all pretty fun characters and it would've been interesting to see what happened to them after Umbrella's fall. 

Despite all of my complaints, I still enjoyed the game, and would recommend it, at least on sale, for any fans of the RE series. Despite its issues ORC can still be an enjoyable shooter, and if you can get 3 other people to play through the game together, you are in for a pretty fun, if somewhat generic, team-based shooter with a good mix of zombie and human enemies.

Really, there are only two types of people who would ever even end up on this game's store page. Maybe you're new to the series, or have played through a number of the main games, and now you're here scraping the barrel for more RE content to sink your teeth into. Maybe you're just curious if it's as bad as everyone says it is, or if it's worth giving a try. In any of these cases, the answer is the same: Yes, it is that bad. No, it's not worth trying.

But maybe you're like me and my friends, misguidedly forcing themselves through bad games to laugh at them. Maybe you're looking for total series completion, at any cost. And perhaps you, the innocent masses, unwashed in the blood we spilled forcing ourselves through this maelstrom of mediocrity, would simply like to know if it's still possible to play this in multiplayer these days.

Well, yeah, kind of. 'Possible' is a strong word.

Wrestling with Games for Windows Live is the first hurdle, sometimes stopping you from even launching the game, because this game is one of the few Capcom games that was never transitioned away from it -- perhaps as a protective barrier of sorts, ensuring that only those truly desperate ever get in to play it. There are guides in the Community section that explain various methods of tricking the software into actually working, but whether they work, and how long they work (one member of our party had to redo it every single time she launched it, because it simply refused to function) are both left largely up to chance. 
Even when you get into the game, it's hardly smooth sailing; several times in our two short playthroughs of each campaign, plot-important monsters would get stuck in a wall and become unkillable, or simply hide out in places the players couldn't actually reach to shoot them, forcing us to either find a way to restart our checkpoint or simply exit to the menu. Sometimes getting a game over will randomly crash members of your party, and on special occasions it may even crash [i]everyone[/i] in the party. This is tolerable in the main campaign, where you can reload the lobby from a checkpoint, but in the DLC campaign (which can, for some reason, seemingly only be played in Free Mode) having to back out to the menu in any way means restarting an entire level. But maybe that's not so bad! What if they're fun, after all?

"But wait! I know where you're going with this!", you say. "You're going to say that it's actually underrated, and fun with friends, right?" 

No. God, no, absolutely not. Why are you even still reading this? ORC is a dull, insipid disaster, from the ground up. The weapons and controls are mostly terrible, the enemies are aggressively spongey and borderline cheat with their aim even on Normal, and the game is loaded with bizarre design choices like making you lose everything in your inventory whenever you go down, or suffering through always-on voice chat that can only be disabled per-person in the party menu, and only [i]before[/i] you've readied up (meaning if a player crashes and has to rejoin, you're stuck listening to them in-game until you've finished the mission). Everything else is just an extremely subpar cover shooter that desperately wants you to think it's something more than that, with character abilities that are all either useless or extremely overpowered and a number of CQC tricks that the game doesn't even tell you about. Presumably because you never have any reason to bother with most of them.

Is the DLC campaign maybe a little bit better? Yeah, I guess. It has an arguably better finale and slightly more presence from classic RE characters, at least, even if they still don't do much. Is it [i]good?[/i] Lord, no. And on top of the overall mediocre presentation, neither campaign is any longer than five short-feeling hours, including crash times and restarts; they attempt to add replay value in the form of collectibles to pad out its paltry length, but fail to realize the simple truth that nobody would ever want to play this game twice.

It's not so bad it's good, and it's only fun with friends in the sense that any game can be with the right group. And on top of both campaigns being non-canon, they're not even canon to [i]each other[/i]. Even if it were, the characters you know and love barely show up in either campaign, despite the game's entire premise being based largely around seeing events of the series from another angle. There's almost no reason to play this, no matter what you're telling yourself. But some of you probably will anyways, because if you're here it's probably because you're unwilling to listen to reason.

[h1]Introduction[/h1]
If you think Resident Evil 6 is a too over the top shooter, well this game comes to prove you wrong. After all the GFWL hassle, what you get is Capcom’s take on the Left 4 Dead formula, a four-person coop third-person arcady shooter. It does not have any Resident Evil classic design like puzzle solving, inventory management etc., just shooting hordes of enemies. In the campaign, you team up with three friends or AI to be a squad of USS (Umbrella Security Service) who help Umbrella cover their evidence or be a squad of government special ops to reveal Umbrella hideous secret (requires DLC). I didn’t play the multiplayer which seems to be a PvPvE deathmatch because today in 2021 this game and GFWL are basically dead. It is very likely you can only stick with AI to play the campaign.

It is the Resident Evil’s take on Left 4 Dead, but it enriches the formula mechanically. Whether you play as USS or special ops, you have six classes to choose from, who have unique abilities but no difference in stats. They probably play a bigger role in multiplayer, but for the campaign, it does not matter much, except for the last two levels in nether special ops campaign you will be much better off playing Willow (recon class). This reflects a very strange and inconsistent level design, since you don’t have to make use of a certain class in the USS campaign and the rest of the special ops campaign (in one level you need demolition class to open gates, but you can easily get away with it using attack from Nemesis).

[h1]The Bad[/h1]
This game only allow you to equip one main weapon and one pistol, and it is a very bad design choice. Since pistol is not very powerful and mainly for emergency purposes, you actually need two main weapons to handle all situations, such as a combo of long and short-range weapons, or regular and high-damage weapons. For example, you need a powerful short-range weapon like a shotgun to blast zombies away in close and sudden contacts, and a sniper rifle to take out snipers. You need regular weapons for normal enemies while reserve a high-damage weapon like RPG or grenade launcher for elites and bosses. My guess is most people end up sticking with a balance mid-range weapon like an AR, which is good but powerless in handling all kinds of different situations. You can of course discard and change to weapons you find any time, but you will soon realize finding certain weapons you needed is a hassle . What's worse, bullets dry out very easily. This severely interrupts the flow of the game as you constantly have to pause from intense fights trying to find bullets or ideal weapons (and also heal and anti-virus spray). 

Additionally, there is no separate sensitivity adjustment for camera movement and aim down sight. You will feel the pain when you have to move your mouse for miles when using a sniper rifle.

[h1]The Very Bad[/h1]
Honestly, I am very mad about the AI. AI in this game is basically broken and dumb as $hit. They don’t group together or move with you (unless you are very far off). They shoot far targets instead of the ones that almost get crawls on them. They block your sight and randomly decide to rush out to knife down enemies. They don’t even deal much damage. Apart from being a distraction, they are just burden. Fortunately, you can leave AI behind if you feel like running away instead of fighting as AI will respawn in the next checkpoint. If the AI is as smart and helpful as that in Left 4 Dead, this game would be so much better.

Japanese developers in PS3/Xbox 360 era usually developed games primarily based on consoles and then transplanted them to PC, and this game is one of the worst transplanted games. The control is really bad and feels off with keyboard and mouse. Movement is as cumbersome and stiff as Resident Evil 6 especially when running, while shooting is way worse and extremely inaccurate. It is very wonky like your aim always lags behind where you aim to, and also feels unpleasantly light, meaning a slight movement can result in a missed shot even I have adjusted sensitivity to the minimum. With the very unstable frame rate and the fact that most weapons in this game have crazy recoil, they made Operation Raccoon City a terrible shooter. With a controller, movement is improved, but I could not work around the inaccuracy.

[h1]The Good (assuming you are a fan)[/h1] 
Now that I get all the bad stuff out of the way, the only good thing that is left is the story. You play as the antagonist, an Umbrella squad, to experience the outbreak in Resident Evil 2 and 3. This story acts as the third perspective (Claire & Leon is the first perspective and Jill is the second) to observe the Raccoon City event, adding some details and explaining (kind of) why some events happened. You meet a few protagonists and villains of the series and some very iconic monsters. In the DLC you play as the special force Echo Six. Echo Six is an outsider so they have nothing to do with the event, just help out the protagonists a bit. Generally speaking, the story is a bit rough, but I like it because it is a great fan service. Therefore, if you are not a fan, it probably does not matter to you.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]
Operation Raccoon City is an terribly transplanted game and a terrible shooter. It does have some ideas but unfortunately fell short. I like the fan service yet it does not appeal to everyone. With the troublesome GFWL, I cannot recommend it to anyone even to die-hard fans. It is just not worthy.

Resident Evil returns to the iconic streets of Raccoon City with this PS3 game. Also moving away from the traditional survival horror roots of the series instead towards a more fast-paced third-person shooter style. This is certainly a fun idea for a spin-off and one that got me very excited back in 2012. When I got my hands on it, however, I was very disappointed as all we ended up with is a below average cover shooter.

Let’s start with the positive points first. Having not seen Raccoon City since the PlayStation 2 it does feel nice to return. Fighting your way through the police station, having to take on Nemesis and chasing down Leon are all very fun and enjoyable ideas. Since Resident Evil 2 or 3 are yet to get a remake in HD like the first game this is the closest fans will get to relive the events of those games. I wish we had a better chance to see Leon and Claire’s escape from Raccoon City or Jill Valentine’s citywide battle with Nemesis. Replaying iconic moments from the original PS1 trilogy now from the other side as Umbrella soldiers sounds like it should be amazing. If these ideas played well I dare say they would be but in the game we got they are sorely lacking. While on the subject of the original trilogy let me ask you a question. What’s your favourite monster from that trilogy? The brutal armoured Hunters? The wall-crawling Lickers? The unstoppable Tyrants? Whatever it is there is a good chance they will be found in this game. The vast diversity of monsters is probably the best thing about Operation Raccoon City. Taking on a number of previous foes or even bosses from the PS1 classics was more fun than it had any right to be in a game this overwhelmingly bad. I would be lying if I didn’t admit that through simple nostalgia and love of monsters like the Crimson heads I didn’t have fun with parts of this game.

Sadly the previous paragraph sums up all the good things about Operation Raccoon City. Now we move on to the much larger subject of the negative points. This is a PlayStation 3 generation game and it looks worse during gameplay than the Resident Evil remake on the Gamecube. Honestly, that’s just shameful. This is made even more obvious when you compare the models for the crimson heads that appear in both games together. On the Gamecube, they have torn skin exposing bloody muscle and jagged bone like claws while on the PlayStation 3 game they are just red zombies. To say I was disappointed with the graphics would be an understatement. Although normally visuals are not something that would ruin a game for me here seeing Raccoon City in HD was one of the biggest selling points. I would recommend Resident Evil Outbreak for any fans that did want to see a beautifully realised Raccoon City through the eyes of a spin-off game.

It’s not just awful visuals as the controls feel even worse. If you’re running and press X then you will dive to the floor but you also have to press X to pick up ammo and other items. This lead to me trying to pick something up only to instead go flying through the air right over the item I wanted and into a crowd of monsters. The shooting itself feels, well just weak. Never once did my weapons feel like they were doing much damage to the enemies I was firing at. Even the human targets would stand there taking shot after shot to the head without even flinching. Every boss and most monsters require no tactics or skill instead just amounting to nothing more than bullet sponges. You’re able to melee enemies but somehow that feels even more ineffective than your guns unless you use your special attack and then it’s overpowered taking down most foes in one hit. Your grenades also feel like they do next to no damage. I bought this game to feel like a bad ass Umbrella soldier like Hunk from the canon but instead, I felt like a kid with a Nerf gun.

Speaking of Hunk from Resident Evil 2 you start the game with him leading your team and this felt amazing but then he dies at the end of the first mission. Your team then proceeds to fail every objective they’re given by Umbrella minus one. I didn’t feel like a badass here, I felt like an ineffective soldier unable to take on any task given to me. The tone is all wrong. None of the characters you follow has any sort of arch or character progression to speak of. For a spin-off non-canonical story the game feels unwilling to take any risks. The events of Resident Evil 2 and 3 are just sort of happening around you. I never felt like I was involved in what was happening at all besides the last boss fight and then even that made no sense. During this final encounter, a few of your team will turn on Umbrella with no reasons given at all. Honestly considering none of them even have a personality that’s not surprising. This is one of the worst stories I have seen come out of the Resident Evil series. When you look back at the amazing stories from not just Resident Evil 2 and 3 but also the Outbreak series it’s almost impressive how the developers seemed to miss every interesting event during this era of the lore. So much could have been done here but instead, it’s a 4-5 hour experience with no atmosphere, character or excitement. If I had to sum this plot up in one word it would be: slog.

If you really loved the original trilogy and the monsters found in those games then maybe pick this up for under a fiver. I mean if you were desperate to kill a weekend it might do because the nostalgia alone lead to me having a little fun but even then you can find better games for that same itch. It’s not terrible but the only thing saving it from that is my nostalgia for the older games so maybe without those rose-tinted glasses this game is terrible. As it stands it was kinda fun to shoot at Lickers, Hunters, Crimson Heads and more for a bit but even that is a flawed experience.

Recommendation Rating: 3 out of 10.

After searching for a halfway decent co op third person shooter game... I always kept coming back here. All of the reviews warn everyone to stay away because of annoying things like GFWL (Games for Windows Live) and the former having a settings.dat file that will auto crash your game on launch like a lot of SEGA games will if you change your display driver. Thankfully half of that battle is over because I did all of that years ago for Lost Planet 2. 

Alright, onto the actual game. 
Resident Evil: Operation Raccoon City is basically Left 4 Dead (Left 4 Dead 2 if you buy the expansion DLCs) meets hero shooter with Currency based unlocks and skills. While you can pick up enemy and player guns, at mission start and on deaths you aren't respawned from leaves you with the loadout you have chosen before the mission start, I haven't seen a side arm drop, but if you have no issue dying and are fine picking up whatever you find on the floor, consider buying one, as most guns don't really come with enough ammo to last you until the next ammo box or crate, and an ammo pile drop rate isn't very high, you might not even have this issue online, but offline, I found myself gravitating towards the Machine gun class because of their huge clip and ammo reserve sizes. 

Gameplay is probably what lured me in the most, along with progression making me feel like I wasn't playing for nothing. There is a fair amount of guns to unlock, 6 players to play as on each campaign I believe, and almost every character has a unique set of passive and active abilities related to their class. Some characters can use infinite ammo for a set time, while others can reduce damage to themselves or an ally for a set time, while others can walk faster or even turn invisible. 
-The RPG style unlock system gives you a lot of reason to keep playing, Found a nice gun on the floor? Died and lost it? Remember the name and save up enough money (EXP it's called) to buy it. Now when you die you just lose grenades and things you picked up during the mission, you also won't have to fight your friends for weapons.

The story, at least from the characters' perspective, makes a lot of sense. Being a mercenary, or what looks like a group of who-evers in the DLC campaign, makes sense. Seeing a group of mercenaries get led on over and over again in an effort to get extracted is a really nice take on people doing questionable things just to go home, and what choices they could make is a very nice take on a co op survival game. 

Mechanically is where the game really drops the champion belt. 
Bleeding attracts zombies, zombies attacking you makes you sick, being sick makes you slowly lose health, and eventually changes you into a zombie. Depending on what shoots or hits you determines your chances of bleeding... Think of bleeding like getting zombie bile on your body like Left 4 dead, zombies will seek you out, try to get you sick, and without a spray skill or specific character skills, you'll die and turn on your teammates 
-The above paired with bad AI teammates and aggressively accurate enemies means that you might be dying a ton on your own, assuming the game is difficult, where the AI on your side might not be tweaked to be useful. 
-Basically at the end stages, you'll be getting hit with that loop happening very often, while you are low on health or ammo, and your teammates died again. 

Some of these controls really suck. The same button that revives teammates, is the same button that picks up ammo, and the same button that has the heel stomp attack when held down. So some of your deaths will just be split second mistakes that had you missing a dive into cover, or getting killed by a turret that makes you bleed, and zombies pop out of nowhere to kill you for having an open wound. And in the main campaign, the last mission is full of that type of chaos. But hey, for 7 dollars with everything it's something I can overlook. 

The formula is very good, but the execution, and the final price leaves this game as something to grab only at times like now, and after you already exhausted the fun out of the title. I see Capcom trying to find the niche to make a crossover game. Where this feels like L4D2, and Resident Evil resistance plays more like a staggered Dead by Daylight. I just hope that if they ever want to do more that they revisit tiles like dragon's Dogma, Lost Planet, and even Devil May Cry. But lets be real, we see how many people still play L4D2, if not for GFWL, maybe people will be more inclined to play this game too. It'll be nice to see more games mix these elements together so nicely.

I don't what it is, but the fact you get to see both sides of the story as the outbreak is happening, and what Umbrella was up to during this time, is exciting in its own way. 

The game takes you across several levels throughout Raccoon City. From the flipped cars on fire streets, to the Nest itself. It gives longtime fans something to appreciate because it pretty much touches base on the all historical locations the series has taken place in. From the police department, hospital, and Dead factory. Of course the layout is different, but it allows this run n' gun, cover shooter shine! On top of that, we even run into main characters from the RE series during their outings through the city. Operation takes place during the events of RE2/3. We speak, and work with, these characters in some missions. Although brief, I really appreciated this! It was fun being on the other side fighting, or teaming up, with the ppl we have played as up to this point in the series. 

As stated, you go in as an Umbrella operative team, on multiple missions to assist Umbrella in covering up their wrong doings. The story is interesting, but does end abruptly. I know this game was not trying to win any award in this regard, but I still wish it was given more time. There will never be a time you're lost with what is going on, but still, I was interested in knowing more.   

You have a decent selection on characters, all with their own unique skill set. If you get the DLC, you will gain access to a new team, but the special abilities stay the same. Find your favorite, upgrade them, and take them through hell and back to try to either, destroy, or save, Raccoon city. After every mission, of course, you get scored on how well you did. There are multiple objectives, from time, to the amount of collectibles you found. All of this tally up, and give XP. XP is spent on unlocking, then upgrading abilities, or weapons. I never counted, but there has to be at least 30, maybe 40 weapons. A great selection to choose form. 

This is actually why I bought the game again, outside the $5 price tag for the complete edition, Operation RC, was one of the very few games I actually played when I was younger. I remember the game had great atmosphere, and the guns didn't sound like pea-shooters. Shotguns, assault rifles, pistols, all have their distinct sound, which I highly appreciate. I am not sure why other Devs have not figured this out? If the guns sound terrible, it takes the pleasure of using it away, imo. But in Operation, unloading a magazine and watching limbs get cut off enemies, head shots blew their heads off, all mixed into a hectic time trying not to be overwhelmed, is an exciting time! I am just glad I was able to capture that again. I was worried the game would turn out much worse, but I am happy to say, it is as I remember. 
Also, just walking / running around sounds good to me. They took their time here, because running on concrete, dirt, gravel, all have their different sounds. And my favorite, is the sound of bullets flying by, and or striking something around you. It helps make it feel more realistic, and grounded, although zombies are trying to bite your face off. 
The only thing I thought was kind of lack luster, was the soundtrack. Not the worst, but you most likely will not even notice it as you play. I turned it down so I could hear my surroundings more. 

The graphics, although dated, to me, still look crisp and hold up. You may know this already, but the screen shots on Steam, do not do it justice. So when I booted it for the first time, I took the time to look around and was happy it wasn't too dated. I am not the biggest on graphics, but I enjoy them when I get them, and I do have a standard. Luckily Operations passed with flying colors! 


Issues,
1. Now, I am not going to lie.... there is some jank.. When it comes to cover, it is old school tactics. Just push forward onto the cover you're trying to hide behind. Issue is, when you do NOT want to cover, but do so anyway. Don't get me wrong, I easily adapted to this, and found my balance, but I know, this will annoy others. 
2. The AI, acts like you would expect from a game this old. Not the worst, but nowhere near the brightest. 
3. You, for some crazy reason, cannot upgrade your team. So as you progress, they, stay the same. Even if you go under X character, and upgrade them, they do not take that into the missions. I think this was to make online more needed then it should be. Obviously you can still beat the game, but this bothered me quite a bit. 
3. STUN LOCK HELL!! Hunters, and Mr T, can knock you down, and if your squad isn't around, or dead, good luck. I always got away, but not before 2/3 hits are in. 

All in all, Operation does feel older, as it is, but still holds up. I had fun! And with the DLC included, you basically double the campaign length. Seeing the Umbrella side is interesting as I stated, just wish more time was given to flesh it out. The sound effects this game has keeps you grounded, and makes it feel like a zombie infested war. I do not want the series to go into this run n' gun genre, but as an outing, does a great job!

NOTE: In order to run the game you need to download GFWL.  Multiplayer both Coop and PvP are unable due to player inactivity.As a fan of the Resident Evil series the idea of running to Raccoon City decked to the teeth in guns and bullets as you lay waste to the undead with heavy machine gun fire is rewarding.  As a "what if" scenario players take on the role of a member of the Umbrella Security Service (USS) sent in to Raccoon City to cover up Umbrella's evil doings, by destroying evidence and killing everything under the sun.  The gimmick is clever for the most part and it is fun to play as the bad-guys for once.  However, the game is fun if you can ignore some of the odd design choices.I like to think that this game was the "progenitor" to future tactical shooters like "The Division" "Ghost Recon" and others as what not too do in making a tactical shooter.  The game is marred with inconsistent A.I., bullet sponged enemies on difficulties higher than NORMAL, and an auto-cover mechanic that gets you stuck in the worst possible situations.  However, with these problems the game is enjoyable, a bleed status and infection status for example, are fun additions where either taking too much damage or causing damage to enemies and cause zombies to go crazy and attack them.  Levels have the proper amount of mood lighting that for an action horror game you still feel like you are in a survival horror game.In terms of customization, the game is robust and limited at the same time.  For instance, the game sports a myriad of different firearms that players can take into battle unfortunately most are useless because with so many enemies on screen at once, it is better to use weapons with high damage output rather than bleed status or high ammo count.  Players can upgrade characters respective status, however, each character is fixed to a type (medic, assault, recon, etc) and the optimization is not there.  It is a shame you cant create the agent you want to make.  Overall, it is a mixed bag, the music is questionable with only a few soundtracks to get the blood pumping.  Guns lack the sound or feeling like you are wasting the dead, odd game-play choices, and yet it is still fun.  Just don't expect players to join you in COOP as hardly anyone plays this game at this time.

This game has had a very bad reputation and only recently I decided to buy since it was 80% discounted thus very cheap. And it is surprisingly... alright.
To get it out of the way: Resident Evil: Operation Raccoon City requires the infamous obsolete Games for Windows Live, but it works! But be warned, [u]it takes a very long time to complete the first login on Games for Windows Live[/u]. It is a shame this game was not updated to remove it, but at least it does not stop us to play this game.
Resident Evil: Operation Raccoon City is a 4-player co-op game (with Versus Mode included) where we control Umbrella operatives part of U.S.S. Delta Team, also callled "Wolfpack". It is not canon, still, this team initially assists HUNK's team to retrieve the G-Virus from William Birkin, as we know things go wrong, Wolfpack is separated from HUNK and has to follow orders from their Command to clean Umbrella's mess on Raccon City. It takes plenty of elements from Resident Evil 2 and 3.
The plot is all over the place. It forces the Wolfpack to encounter other known characters from Resident Evil and also enemies, and previous bosses (G-Birkin, Mr. X and even Nemesis) with feeble justifications for their introduction and exit. Even Ada Wong is thrown into the plot for no good reason. There was a lot of wasted potential with the characters from Wolfpack. All 6 available have interesting backstories and have interesting personalities (dialogues change depending on which characters are chosen), but are not vey explored with lack of closure. It would be nice to have them inserted on the canon of Resident Evil. Instead of a side story, Capcom opted for a non-canon plot putting as many non-canon cameos as possible, sadly. There are 2 possible endings but again none are canon.
The graphics are quite decent. Sure they are not as detailed as other Resident Evil games, but simulate well Raccon City. since it is an action game, the scenarios are bright and basically all areas are larger than usual despictions in the main games.
The soundtrack is very good and also on par with the rest of the franchise.
The gameplay was adapted from consoles and do not translate very well for mouse and keyboard. It is practically impossible to use the "dodge" button since it is placed on "E". The rest of the controls work well enough. We choose 4 of 6 available operatives, all from different classes with their own active and passive abilities. To unlock them and new weapons, XP enough is required to be available in-between missions. Though it is possible to freely change weapons throughout the levels. There is cover but is automatic and not possible to vault. The shooting works well though there is not much impact on enemies, who often behave as "sponge bullets", it is quite unpolished. The teammates controlled by AI are definitely useful, but we can't direct them so they are hit-and-miss.
There are also several "data" to collect throught the scenarios, encouraging exploration which increase the ranking of the Chapter giving more XP but alro unlocking interesting Concept Arts to view.
The ammo depletes quite fast and we must always be wary of the health; an interesting mechanic is that if a AI or human player dies infected it becomes zombie forcing the others to defend from it.
The campaign is very short. I only took about 4 hours to finish the whole campaign. It wasn't shorter because I died in a few parts with waves of enemies, especially on the finale. The game is designed for replay to get extra XP to unlock Abilities and Weapons for all operatives, but the campaign does not have steam for replaying it so many times, unless you play it other prople, but expectedly is rare to find other players to play with.
A very inconvenient problem is the game only saves between chapters. There are checkpoints, but if you leave the game you have to restart the whole chapter, which is very bad. Fortunately the game is short, so it shouldn't be too much problem.
Though there is a separate campaign, with a team called "Echo Six" more focused on Jill, Carlos and Nemesis appearances, only the Prologue is free, and is only playable from "Free Play" menu. There is a bug which impeded me to finish this mission. The rest of this "Echo Six" campaign is [b]paid[/b], which I do not recommend to buy unless is very cheap, though I do know is even shorter than "Wolfpack" campaign.
So, since I paid very little and had low expectations with Resident Evil: Operation Raccon City I managed to actually like this game for what it offered. It definitely had a big potential as a co-op shooter spin-off which was very wasted with bad design and creative choices, as well a flagrant lack of polish and replayability. But with low expactations it becomes a fast entertainment to appreciate.

Recuerdo allá hace unos nueve años cuando escuché por primera vez la premisa de este juego: Sos parte de un grupo especial de Umbrella, similar al que pertenecía Hunk el cuarto superviviente de Resident Evil 2, encargado de destruir evidencia y supervivientes en medio de el ataque zombie en Raccoon City y entre medio te cruzas con personajes como Jill, Leon, Claire, Carlos y Nicholai, entre otros. INCREÍBLE. No solo eso, el hecho de POR FIN poder jugar como los malos era una idea demasiado tentadora para poder pasarla, pero hay mas! El juego también te da la posibilidad de jugar una campaña completa como un equipo especial del gobierno estadounidense, Echo Six, encargado de buscar toda la información posible para poder imputar a Umbrella por lo sucedido. Absolutamente increíble.
 Doce personajes jugables, dos campañas diferentes, de vuelta en Raccoon City con zombies, aparte de eso multijugador, volvieron los lickers, los hunters, Nemesis, Mr. X, Crimson Heads, los soldados tienen cada uno habilidades dependiendo de su rol en el escuadrón, tenés un impresionante accionar a tu disposición. Nada puede fallar! Bueno...
 La idea del juego es FANTÁSTICA para todo fanático de la saga. Vengo jugando estos juegos desde el primero allá por principios del 98 cuando era demasiado jovencito para hacerlo y el ver que una idea tan genial haya sido ejecutada con tantos errores me rompe el corazón. Vayamos por partes, dijo Jack:

-LO MALO: 
 El port de consola a PC es una aberración, los controles son un desastre y el juego no te explica NADA. Como tomas de escudo a un zombie? Suerte mirando una guia online porque ni en pedo te lo dicen. Con qué botón cambiás de granadas? Jodete y buscalo vos. Con qué me curo? Toqueteá hasta que encuentres. Y así con todo, tranquilamente podes pasar veinte minutos tocando el teclado hasta que encuentres lo que necesitás y mas o menos la piloteas pero es atroz.
 Los gráficos están mas o menos. Para la época iban bien pero hoy en día se notan bastante génericos, no malos, pero genéricos. Los personajes principales, sin embargo, están excelentemente hechos con texturas espectaculares en los chalecos y detalles como granadas colgando o cintitas en los brazos, la verdad sorprende habiendo sido desarrollado hace casi una década y para PS3 y XBOX 360.
 Las animaciones y la historia se sienten como que tuvieron muy poco tiempo de cocción y fue todo a las apuradas. A veces aparecen monstruos medio de la nada y sin explicación (como Nemesis en la fundición) o suceden cosas que te las dicen pero no te las muestran y te quedas tipo "ok..." y no te queda otra que aceptar que pasó. O te introducen a un personaje que no te explican quién es, o por qué tiene un uniforme de otro color o un arma diferente, simplemente aparece, lo matas y seguis lo mas campante sin que nadie haga un solo comentario. Esto sobre todo en la campaña de Echo Six en donde los personajes se parecen a Bernardo del Zorro de lo mudos que son en un claro contraste con la campaña de The Pack (los soldados de Umbrella) que hacen comentarios cada uno acorde a su personalidad y se la nota mas trabajada en general.
 Luego también el tema del CQC con el cuchillo es un despojo de Satán. Si tuvieras una pared de ladrillo enfrente no le pegarías, básicamente. Funciona de la siguiente manera: Apretás el botón y el personaje hace una cadena de ataques con cuchillo en dirección recta hacia donde estés indicandole sin importar si el enemigo se movió en el medio (pasa todo el tiempo) o se corrió de alcance luego del primer golpe (pasa todo el tiempo) así que te quedás tirando manotazos al aire como una gallina que recién se levanta mientras los enemigos te rellenan como empanada santiagueña o los zombies te cagan a tarascones, es un desastre.
 Por último está el correr. Cuando apretás el botón de sprint el personaje corre con la delicadeza de Macri hablando sobre los derechos de las mujeres. Te chocás contra todo, tenés cero maniobrabilidad, vas a lo bestia y cuando te das cuenta de que tenés que parar estás en medio de una horda zombie que ya te puso entre dos panes o en un cuarto lleno de soldados todos preguntandote que qué tal se ve el cañon de sus escopetas.
 Algunas de las exageraciones típicas del género de acción para hacer quedar cancheros a los personajes me hacen girar los ojos hasta que pegan la vuelta y detesto que sigan poniendo a Hunk como si fuese Schwarzenegger (Esaaa, lo escribí sin googlear). Es la misma razón por la que detesto a Vector, es el cancherito que le gusta a todos los niños rata. Aguanten Lupo y Beltway.
 Ah, Carlos tiene alta cara de bobo.

-LO BUENO:
 Los personajes en general son carismáticos (más si viste los trailers) y todos tienen algo que le va a apelar a alguien. Bertha y Beltway destacando de entre The Pack, sin dudas.
 El juego es absolutamente único en su premisa dentro de esta franquicia y es un soplo de aire fresco entre el RE 4 matando españoles con las plagas (como odio ese juego), el 5 con Chris todo papoteado, el 6 con Leon haciéndole competencia a Bruce Willis etc.
 La premisa es el sueño mojado de todo fan viejo de Resident Evil y cumple en muchos aspectos. Te cansás de recorrer Raccoon City en dos campañas diferentes viendo cuerpos con algunos de los mayores gore de la franquicia (vas a ver intestinos, cuerpos decapitados, brazos arrancados etc) cosa que hasta el 2012 cuando salió no se había hecho en este detalle.
 Los gráficos a veces sorprenden por su detalle sobre todo cuando peleas en la oscuridad y realmente te da miedo porque no sabés cuántos zombies te rodean, sobre todo en dificultades altas.

 Super divertido si tenés algo de paciencia por sus errores y si le ponés el mod "destroy everything" que hace que las armas sean mas reales, sino los zombies literalmente son esponjas de balas.

A white crow in the pack- Operation Raccoon City is a spinoff to RE:2 and 3 respectively, taking a look at the tragedy of Raccoon City from the side of those  partially responsible for it- Umbrella Security Service.

Taking the role of any member of team Delta (reconstituted after the events of RE:0) you can clear the way through almost all the iconic locations of Raccoon City, which are made with great detail. 
The plot is obviously very solid. The whole idea of being able to see the outbreak through the lens of the gas masks of Umbrella operatives is very creative and doesn't fail to deliver a good enough storyline with multiple callbacks to the original games. 
It's quite short, but it's good.
The coop portion of the game also really good (taking into account the enourmous stupidity of bots), but you will need an hour to set it up because of GWFL issues. There's a guide on Steam you can use to do it, shouldn't be much of a problem.
The visuals (despite the obvious reasoning for overall quality of the game being relatively low) look and feel very good, capturing the decadent atmosphere of a citywide outbreak*. I have some questions about some of the character's models, but they will never be answered regardless.
The voiceover is very good and I found it very strange, that Capcom who were overseeing the development, never took the entire project down a more storytelling lane. But, the game went through a harsh development cycle, so...

Them bugZ. Occasional bad scripting and possible exploits include: clearing enemies from afar when they fail to respond; Spoilers ahead: Nicholai acting rather strange in both of his bossfights; and the best of the best- the Tyrant freezing in the multiplayer mode.

The Echo Six campaign is half as good as the Wolfpack's. The characters are cringy, missions are mostly very dull (and God I hated the invincible U.S.S soldiers which instakill you), but they make it up with some very interesting moments that include the original characters, locations and events.
Overall, the game is pretty solid. Not as good as other games of the series, but it's obvious.
Grab some friends and play through the campaigns a couple of times. It's worth it.   6.5/10
