RE:ORC is considered by many to be objectively the worst entry in the RE franchise, and the reviews for this game should show it. Many of the reviews however, focus on the difficulty of actually running the game. The game IS broken, and requires a fix. But the problem is that the fix takes a total of 2-3 minutes. Focusing on that issue takes attention away from the more important aspects of why this game is terrible regardless of it being a broken port.
In what follows, I have broken my opinion down into seven different categories, so judgement can be easier.

Story: 4/10
I'm not going to go into full detail here, but the story is acceptable. It's not good, but it's one of the better aspects of the game, which really isn't saying much.
The story is acceptable in the sense that I expected Umbrella to act the way it did in this game. Playing for the bad guys for once sounds like a good idea on paper, but this game doesn't do anything right. It had a ... presentable ... premise that was messed up by a team of unmerciful developers.

Characters: 2/10
You play as a faceless soldier of your choice. They all play out pretty much the same, and their special abilities do not hinder or help you nearly as much as they should. It's kind of fun to play as a supposed badass, but when the game doesn't have the courage to render their faces, why should I care for any of the exchangeable, expendable characters?
That's the point. You don't care. The game fails to create any kind of sympathy for its characters, nor does it even try.
Remember the RE movies and the oh-so-memorable characters who died ten minutes after they were introduced, leaving you to wonder why you even bothered learning their names? That's how much effort the game developers put into character design and development for RE:ORC.

Gameplay: 1/10
There is nothing spectacular, extraordinary, or even good about how the game plays out. Hearing some mission objectives might sound fun during the briefings, but any facade of them being fun is thrown away the moment the mission begins.
RE:ORC is in no way a horror game and has the absolute minimal traces of horror, it's quite action-oriented. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but this game has no idea how to make a fun action game. The action can be summed up as the player struggling to have fun.

Graphics: 4/10
Don't get me wrong. The models and the environments look nice. That is, if the constant darkness actually let you see them. RE and RE2 took place during the night, so did RE3, so did the majority of RE4, and RE2:Remake. Those games were gorgeous for their time. Despite the darkness, you could see the characters, the environments, the enemies, and cherish the amount of work put into them.
It's actually incredible how the developers managed to fubar darkness. I'm actually amazed how the developers managed to screw up by doing absolutely nothing. Flat out incredible how a thing they didn't even do still managed to make this game worse.

Sound effects: 2/10
The soundtrack is absolute garbage even raccoons wouldn't come close to (pun intended). Voice acting is ... alright, I guess. The sound effects themselves are pretty dull.
My main issue with the game is that it's incredibly loud. It hurts my ears just to play this game for more than ten minutes. The loudness can be compared with a COD title.

Control: 1/10
Clunky, hard, and designed to test humanity's patience.

Play value: 1/10
It's just ... not ... fun. It's painful in every sense of the word to play this game.

Overall score: 2/10
Comparable to "Dino Crisis 3".

Final verdict: Do yourselves a favor, and stay away from this game unless your life depended on it. I bought it on sale for $5, and I regret my decision every day. Sadly I wasn't aware of the time, and played for almost 100 minutes. Bye bye, money.

RE: Operation Raccoon City was released in 2012 for both the Xbox 360 and PS3. It is a great non-canon game that features two different perspectives to the Raccoon City outbreak. On one side you have Umbrella's team Delta and the United States team Echo Six. RE: ORC features 12 playable characters with both teams having characters with their own special focus (/ability). Each member has their special perk which makes it fun no matter who you play. One example of a perk is the scientist's ability which gives you a 'pheromone grenade' that allows you to draw zombies where you throw it, very useful in the online games when you want to draw them to your enemies. 

The story focuses on the outbreak and lets you see fan-favorite characters interact with these players. Depending on which side you play, you could end up killing Leon/Claire or helping to save them. The games gives you the ability to use zombies as meat shields and has a greater focus on melee combat. While the solo games are very fun to play with friends and even online, the multiplayer is where you will spend hours playing. 

The multiplayer modes consist of team Deathmatch, Biohazard, survivors, and Heros mode. Deathmatch is exactly what it sounds like. Survivors mode pits you against the opposing team as you wait for a helicopter to arrive and whisk you off to safety. Biohazard mode will have you fighting for samples of the G-virus while Heros mode allows you to play as your favorite characters, like Hunk or Jill.

For anyone still interested in trying it out but suffering from the startup crashes or inability to play/save due to the GFWL, there's an extremely easy work around that doesn't require you to install or reinstall anything like some of the unnecessarily long guides out there might tell you. For the crashes I just went into the steam folder and changed the games application compatibility to Windows 7 and boom I never had any problems again. For GFWL, all you have to do is click 'create account' scroll down and check the fine print at the bottom, you'll see a clickable bit of highlighted text that allows you to create a local profile that remembers you every time you open and close the game. Each time you open a new instance it'll ask you to log in but just close the interface down because it'll always automatically log your local profile in and in turn, allow saving.
If you love RE games, this is a must have.

A friend of mine gifted me this game so that we could play this .. thing, and have fun mocking it in the process. Kinda how you would watch a movie like Sharknado just to laugh about how bad it is.
So far we've had decent fun in that regard, but I chose to make this review serious. This game is really bad, and really doesn't have anything going for it. Here's everything:

- GAME INSTALL: First off, you have to earn the right to play this game by working on it a little bit. You have to download an installer for a thing named "Game for Windows Live" which is some sort of "ancient-Steam-like-program" that has been completely decommissioned since then. Installing this thing will be complicated and messy. You'll have to research for the whole process on the web. So if you're expecting to buy and play it instantly to blow off some steam, avoid this game.

- MUSICS: The first thing that will greet you when you start the game is an atrocious main menu music. So atrocious that even someone that doesn't know a thing about music will notice. It actually hurts your ears, not even kidding. Besides that, every music in the game is so forgetable I don't remember any of it.

- GRAPHICS: This game came out in 2012. For comparison, Dishonored 1, Borderlands 2, Mass Effect 3, Assassin's Creed 3, and finally FarCry 3 all came out in the exact same year. It would be very fair and even a little forgiving to say this game looks like a PS2 game. Even games like Half-life 2, which came out five years before, looks much better in comparison. That alone is just for textures. Moving on with animations, those are laughably pathetic, most of the time recycled throught the game, that would make an SFM amateur feel like Pixar in comparison. Even cutscenes are bad ! .. What did I say ? Cutscenes are ESPECIALLY bad !

- GAMEPLAY: So, huh .. You walk in places and you shoot things. That's almost all there is to it. There are several characters you can choose from, and all of them have access to special abilities and perks. Almost all of them are going from unremarkable to useless, so your guns and regular shooter skills are your main source of damage and utility in this game. Speaking of guns, they are, just like abilities, unlockable with XP as you play. They do not seem to be very balanced and there are definite clear "Better" and "Worse" weapons. You can also swap weapons during a mission. Besides that, you have to watch for your health, ammo, and other states like bleeding, which is caused by enemy soldier weaponry, and deals damage over time. Or infection, which is caused by zombies and will deal damage over time ( And eventually turn you into a zombie ! ) until healed. Ammo is replenished with .. ammo. Health is replenished with green herbs and green sprays. Infection is removed with anti-viral sprays. Both sprays can be applied to both you and any teammates around you if they are close. Here you go, that's all there is to it. Besides that, you can revive dead teammates. Even if they got infected, turned into a zombie, and lost limbs in the process. If you don't have viral sprays, you can also put a bullet in your friend's head before picking him up, too, as friendly fire is enabled, and rewarded through points in this case. That alone is relatively funny. 

Other than this, you can also dodge things by throwing yourself on the ground, by pressing E when sprinting. This will never be useful to actually dodge and will just screw you up when trying to pick up something while sprinting for the first time. You can also pick zombies as meatshield against enemy soldiers, and since soldiers are problematic ( I will get to this in my review ) It's incredibly useful if you can manage to do it. Other than this, you can also perform finishers after melee-ing any enemy. It's not farfetched to say that the gameplay is bland, stale and boring. Don't buy this game if you're looking for oustanding, breath-taking game design.

DIFFICULTY: So, huh, no matter in what difficulty setting you are, you will notice something. Zombies are cannon fodder and are easily dispatched ( Unless you are in a very tight spot ) and enemy human soldiers in comparison are THE REAL DEAL. The second they spawn in, if you are a fraction of a second out of cover, your health bar will instantly be annihilated and you will die in a matter of seconds. The "cover" system is simple. Simply walk towards a potential conver and your character will crouch behind it. While it works on paper, the system will make you want to tear your hair from your head because of how bad it is handled. You will sometimes fire or even blind-fire into the cover itself, your character will fire from the wrong side or angle, and throwing grenades from the left side will get you killed from your own explosives, since characters solely throw them from their right hand, throwing them into the wall. This also result in your character standing up and getting shot. No blind throws. In fact, I am pretty sure there is no special animations for throwing a grenade under cover. Your character just perform its "out of cover" Grenade animation then ducks back underneath. 

This alone would never be a problem if the AIs were all dumb, but the problem is, the devs were very keen on making enemy humans feel "realistic". They will target you even if you are under cover, if a slight portion of your body is exposed, with the accuracy of a CS:GO player. But since covers are usually broken cars, concrete blocks or even fences if you're unlucky, you will be shot from god-knows-where and die. Fortunately for you, there is a lot of checkpoints, and besides this the AI is still rock stupid. So you will manage to progress in the game after dying several time on that one sequence that is unusually difficult and annoying. And this, again, in all difficulty levels.

Besides regular zombies and soldiers, you will meet other enemies from the Resident Evil franchises. Ranging from Lickers, Hunters, Tyrans, Bosses from other games like Nemesis or Birkin, and .. Headcrabs from HalfLife ? Because yes, there are some kind of weird, insectoid Headcrabs that are featured in no other Resident Evil Games. Coming back to those enemies and bosses I was talking about, how are they special ? Well, it depends on how much you enjoy fighting mentally-challenged bullet sponges. We dealt with it relatively easily on our side. That includes bosses which are sometimes so easily destroyed they almost humiliate their incredible appearances in actual Resident Evil games.

PLOT, STORY AND WRITING: This game is not cannon to the Resident Evil universe. If you go throught the game, you will understand why. The entirity of the plot feels like a bad, cringy fancfiction written by a 10 years old Resident Evil fanboy. Featuring nonsensical scenes to justify incoming waves of enemies, bland and unoriginal characters, clichés and stereotypes everywhere, evil commanders that betrays you, but also gets bullied by their own soldiers and acts like children. I could delve into details but I really don't want to. There is so much to write but yet, so little to say about it. It really does feel like a bad fanfiction.

If you are somebody that enjoys hearing character voicelines and chat in the game to learn more about their stories and developpement, you are also going to be incredibly disappointed. Everything is either cliché, nonsensical, or ... nobody talks. Yeah, that's a thing too. Sometimes character do not say a single word besides the crazyness of what just happened. And sometimes they will have some cringy dramatic monologue while another one cuts them mid-sentence to say something alike "♥♥♥♥, I NEED AMMO !". This game is far from being the only game doing this, but it happening relatively often is just icing on the cake.

CONCLUSION: Is this game bad ? Yes ! It is "So bad it's good" ? Absolutely ! If you delve into this game with this in mind, then you will probably end up "enjoying" it like we did.

Resident Evil: Operation Raccoon City was released on PC, May 18, 2012. Though this game has been out for 7 years, it is still an awesome experience. I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the Resident Evil stories, and who isn't concerned about it being the classic survival horror. This game is 3rd person but can be 1st person when aiming with a sniper rifle. It is more action than anything, but definitely has its fair share of jump scares during certain parts of the game. This has become one of my favorite Resident Evil games because it is set between Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 3. You even "return" to the Raccoon City Police Department. It is all too familiar to those of us who played Resident Evil 2 when it was released, or not long after. 

The composer, Shusaku Uchiyama, did magnificent work with the soundtrack for the game. It keeps you on your toes and adds to the intensity of the game, as well as its eeriness. When you get inside the Main Hall of RPD, if you listen carefully to the music, you can hear the recognizable notes from the original soundtrack to Resident Evil 2 "The Front Hall", somewhat creeping about in the "Police Department" track. It is very nostalgic and takes you back to those days of playing RE2. Listen to RE: ORC track 23 "Police Department" and you will experience nostalgia with RE2 like never before. Compare it to the RE2 track 11 "The Front Hall".

You can play as the Umbrella Security Service (USS) (bad guys) or Spec Ops Command "Echo Six" (good guys). Both have unique campaigns and can be played in solo or co-op. Plenty of missions to do, zombies to kill, and bosses to take down. You might even meet Nemesis. ;) There is also Versus, where you can play several different multiplayer modes. There is a rank structure for your profile, and when you acquire XP, it progresses your rank, no matter which characters you use, or what game mode.

The problem with this game is that it is underrated. I believe a lot of people would enjoy it more if they had not encountered the "Games For Windows Live" issues. Then, there is the percent of hardcore RE fans who just prefer the classic survival horror. Personally, I enjoy all of the games I've played, including this one. The GFWL issue definitely did not help and made most, including myself, stop attempting to play the game, due to all of the login issues. Then one day I decided to research more and see if I couldn't find a fix for the issue. Most of the resolutions that had been posted on YouTube or on forums, were dated. I found a forum on Steam that looked promising and I tried it. Before I knew it, I was playing the game without issues. 

It was fresh in my mind, so I decided to create a YT video on this fix so that others, like myself, could attempt to fix the problem and play the game they so desired. Especially after all of us spent the money on it. This game could also be called "Missed Opportunity: The Game". I think that the idea of playing as an Umbrella squad that is sent to Raccoon City to wipe out evidence is interesting, but the execution here is just poor.

The story is okay taken in consideration that it's not canon (since the game changes some events from RE 2 and 3) and there are some decent moments here and there, but overall the game is just not fun.

Gunplay is terrible, human enemies will often not even flinch when you shoot them and a lot of enemies in the game are just bullet sponges. Human enemies can also cause a lot of damage and sometimes cause some unexpected deaths since they drain your HP quickly if they're close enough - and if you're playing alone, you can revive the AI but the AI can't revive you, so dying is back to the last checkpoint. The AI is also awful, often getting in the way of your shooting or standing in doorways when you're trying to walk through. Enemy AI is also not great and I've seen a few enemies just standing in place, including one boss that just stood there taking shots to the head from every direction.

The game encourages some exploration, but not too much - sometimes you can find extra supplies or data for extra XP, but often you'll just run into rooms that are completely empty.

Enemy encounters can sometimes be pretty ridiculous with the game throwing way too much stuff at you all at once, which is made worse from the fact that some enemies can knock you down repeatedly, leaving you unable to do anything. Boss encounters are either fighting bosses that are massive bullet sponges or the game forces you to use specific mechanics in order to beat them. One offender in specific was incredibly frustrating as I had to lure the boss to being under a cauldron with some molten liquid and activate a machine to pour it on the boss, except I had to lure the boss AND run to activate the lever because of course the AI doesn't do either of those, then do that again two more times AND also fight a massive wave of zombies at the same time too.

Two things worth mentioning is that I played the Scout using a skill to turn invisible, but sometimes enemies would spot me even though I was invisible. The second thing is that I once got stunlocked when fighting two Tyrants, they got me stuck in a corner spamming a knockdown move so I could only sit and watch, the damage was also minor so it'd take forever to kill me. I only managed to stay alive because the AI killed one of them before I died.

I guess this game would be more fun to play with friends, but I don't see any reason to do it when there are much better games to play together. Plus, between the two campaigns and versus mode, there's also very little replay value.

Take a hard pass on this one.

First of all this game suffers from using GFWL that honestly should be removed if they're selling this game on Steam. You can still play it though on Windows 10 by installing a GFWL redistributable and logging in to GFWL, but it's a pain (a dealbreaker for most, and I agree). It even has achievements, but only on GFWL (UGH!).

Second, this is not a Resident Evil game. This is a Left 4 Dead cover-based shooter type of 
 game that happens to be in the Resident Evil universe while also violating its canon (you revisit the events of RE2 and RE3). So if you were expecting some type of survival horror then you're going to be disappointed (goodbye to that feeling of horror and desesperation when you see a hunter come after you for the first time). This is a game where you kill hordes of zombies and also fight against other soldiers (that can rip you to pieces in seconds, yeah) in a campaign that's around 7 hours long plus a 6 hour long DLC campaign.

When playing solo, you are accompanied by 3 squad members each with their unique abilities although their AI can be hilariously bad sometimes. Ammo and healing items are plentyful (maybe not that much on harder difficulties) and you can find guns laying around (you can only carry one "big" gun and one pistol at a given time).

Some bosses can stunlock you and some monsters can get stuck in walls, but it's all part of the hilariously bad experience.

With that said, you can genuinely have fun with this game by just mowing down hordes of zombies with your guns and abilities while trying to fight Umbrella's classical B.O.W. (that go a bit over the top in this game honestly). You can maybe have some fun with your friends too (it has a multiplayer mode but I didn't try it).

If you just want to kill some zombies, revisit some classic RE scenarios and characters, have the guts to fight GFWL and you see this game steeply discounted, then yeah you should give it a try. If you say no to one of the previous statements, please stay the hell away from this game because it's not worth it.

Operation Raccoon City is a fun game, but where it shines is its coop campaign. You play as one of several operatives with two passive abilities and three active ones, though you can only pick one active ability at a time. There is a range of primary weapon and even sidearms which allow a person to run most any playstyle. The unique operators also have their own personalities, such as a half mad german medical doctor, a curious and cold field scientist, and even an ex-USSR intelligence officer.

As an example of their unique abilities I will run down the field scientist, "four-eyes". She has two passive abilites, the first being to carry extra anti-viral sprays (more useful than you think), and the second is biometric vision which allows you to assess an enemy's health and where they exact weakspot is. While it's natural to assume where weakspots are, knowing is better than guessing. She also has three active abilities, the first allowing her to induce infection in humans and zombies that turns them into allies, the second is a gas cload grenade that paints anything inside it as a target for the infected, and last is essentially a target override gun that turn enemy infected into commandable allies.

That is just one character though, and there are 6 in the base game. As for the elephant in the room, GFWL. It's crap. It's always been crap. Now that it's practically defunct it's even more crap than it used to be...but...it's not unfixable. Fixing it requires anywhere between 30 minutes to an hour, is tedious, and can be frustrating, but I firmly believe that the game was worth the time and effort to fix, meaning I recommend it. There are guides and discussions about how to get the game running, so be sure to check there for help on getting it running. 

When the game works it's fun, when you play it with friends even moreso. I do suggest playing on either veteran or professional, simply for the fact that enemies will terrify you, and your fireteam will be just as vulnerable to each other as to the enemies. All this being said, I think moving to steamworks would revitalize this game, help scrub that mostly negative rating (which is mostly due to GFWL), and make the possibility of an operation raccoon city 2 all the more appealing to Capcom. I'll say my last piece and be done with it: The world needs more fun coop campaign games, they're a dying breed and are far too often forgotten in favor of horde mode or multiplayer.

I think it says a lot about this game that, while it's far from my favorite RE game, I really hope they find a way to incorporate the characters from it into the RE2 remake in some way. They've got a surprising amount of personality and help add a face to the otherwise uninteresting USS (HUNK excluded of course). The fact that there are still mods to add these characters to other games all these years later (the most notable of which is the XCOM 2 mod) says a lot.

My only real gripe about this game is honestly the fact that they came so close to making it canon. If they'd just held off on the fan-service a little bit more, we could have had an awesome addition to the mainstream RE universe. But instead, we're going to have to settle for an interesting alternate take on the events of RE2 and 3. This is of course unless Capcom decides to incorporate Wolfpack into the RE2 remake in some way (I mean, they used the "Home of Umbrella" sign that this game added, so I can hope).

Why do I still want to give this game a thumb up? ... to be honest, I don't know.
Maybe it's the charme of the game, maybe the fun we had in coop.
The game is so badly designed, it's always funny to laugh about it and actually, the game uses some nice ideas.

But to get you prepared, what awaits you: Enemies with Instant Aimbot, Bulletsponges, Silent Cutscenes, Copy Paste Boss Enemies, Boss enemies you can take control with one of your special abilities (So broken!), Bad Voice Acting, A Russian Umbrella Dude with a Snail Mask, another Evil Russian Dude walkting towards the camera in front of an explosion in slow motion, Broken melee combat, funny game controls.

So now to the nice stuff: 
This game is a full package of Resident Evil stuff. You will see so many iconic faces and enemies in this game that you will think every 30 minutnes "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this dude is here?!".
I like the Zombies in this game, their movement looks good and they are actually dangerous (Not as completly broken as the enemy Aimbot Soldiers)
You got 6 different Characters to play, each one with their own special abilities and some of them are surprisingly innovative. You get your typical Medic, Assault and Explosives Classes, but also a stealthy class, then the king of the minimap with a more detailed map and better vision modifications and of course my personal favourite class, the Scientist, who can take control of up to 5 Infected Enemies, even the toughest of them and also Minibosses. This is so gamebreaking but also a lot of fun :D.
Each class got 2 passive and 3 active abilities, so there is more you can get for each class.
You can also choose your favourite weapon loadout and there is a lot to choose and even more, if you got the dlc bundles.

I would even recommend playing on easy for the most satisfyingly gunplay (headshots actually kill the first shot!)

There is also a second campaign with different characters, but same classes. I only played the first chapter, because it is free and the rest is DLC. The length was insane compared to the Main Campaign, but I think it was because of the difficulty (Recommend time to finish 30minutes, we took 70minutes, 20 minutes alone for the Boss fight).

So all in all, a "Funny because it's bad" - Coop Experience, which can work well, if you are into that kind of stuff, but BEWARE the Struggle of actually getting this game to work!

I'll preface this by saying, this game isn't anything spectacular. Hell the base version of the game probably leans toward bad rather than anything else, but I really like it.

Firstly, don't get it unless it's discounted. I've bought this game three times due to some unexplainable love (or mental deficiency), and I honestly feel that when I paid £6.00 for the version with all DLC I was playing the real game for the first time.

There are two stories, one where you play as Umbrella covering up the outbreak in Racoon City by sabotaging the city and destroying evidence. It's a servicable campaign with a lot of "collectables" in classic Resi fashion. The second story is the DLC and is *not* included in the base version, hence why you should wait till its only sale to buy the complete edition. This story is basically the other side of the game, and has you playing as a Spec Ops squad trying to do...well the opposite of the main campaign.

Honestly it's kinda scummy especially with how the Triple Impact Trailer (Awesome Trailer BTW) featured both squads *before* the game came out, meaning essentially the base game is only half the experience. The main campaign is short and can be finished in 5- 6 hours, although I'd argue it has replayability. When you add the second campaign you can bump it to 12+ which is arguably average for a shooter nowadays.

So what is it and why after all that do I like it? Well its a Socom style game set in the Resident Evil universe. Specifically during Resident Evil 2. You play as part of a four man squad (with six playable characters per campaign) and face a combo of zombies, generic soldiers, and special B.O.W.'s. You'll need to rely on your teammates and each character's special abilities to survive each level, meaning the game is obviously best played on Co-op. But even so, the single player is actually pretty good and the AI are actually fairly competent.

The general combat is pretty standard. You point you shoot you use cover etc etc. Movement is a little sluggish and actually feels slightly rooted in the modern resi style, even though it's a lot more accomodating to...well actually yknow moving around. Honestly it feels like a very typical third person shooter at its core, and its not neccessarily a bad thing. It doesn't push the genre in any real way, and borrow most of its mechanics from other co-op games and the main series itself, but the combination is actually pretty solid when all's said and done.

The level design is good in some parts and questionable in others. One thing that I feel makes the game unique is the fact the levels can feel very oppressive, making difficult situations even more intense. This isn't always good though, as the opression is sometimes just a case of shortsighted design, or cheap choke points and traps which just don't feel fun to play in. The general balance though leans towards good, and the environments manage to keep some semblance of variety even if the setting isn't massively interesting.

Story wise the game is decent. Hell maybe even good if you're a resi fan (or bad if you're a resi fan). The game shows a side of resi we haven't really saw before, and allows us to enter the setting with a lot more tools at our disposal than usual. You won't be all that surprised by the general narrative, but the experience is interesting enough to keep most fans playing. If you don't like resident evil, it still holds up, but don't expect anything magnificent.

Overall the game is a fairly standard third person shooter, with enjoyable co-op and a certain charm and atmosphere that can overshadow a fair amount of its flaws. It's not a great game, and a lot of it feels like it could have been fleshed out a lot more. But it's also not terrible.

Is it worth full price? No.

Is the base game worth buying? No.

Is it worth buying on sale with DLC? Yes.

So in conclusion, although its maybe not the kind of recommendation that will make you want to buy it, I can genuinely recommend the complete edition when its reasonably priced. It's not a cult classic, it'll never get a sequel, hell Capcom will never even admit it exists at this point, but it has one thing going for it. 

It's fun. With friends it's even more fun.

I will say this, this game is underrated. The marketing for the game was great and so were the trailers. I will not spoil the game but i will summarize the key things that everyone should know. Below is my brutal honest review of RE: Operation Raccoon City..

You play as the Umbrella Special Forces squad, The Wolfpack. Umbrella sent a team of elite soldiers to go clean up their mess before the world knows that Umbrella caused this. Each soldier has their own set of unique skills that they offer to the team. Essentially, you play as the bad guys in this RE game. First, it does have some survival horror aspect but, it's mostly action horror. The amount of ammo they give you is fair and you can play up to three other people with you. You will encounter some old areas in the past RE games and some rather... old faces. This game is most behind of the scenes. So, in reality, the game takes place between RE2 and RE3 (that should give you an idea of what to expect). In the DLC's, you play as the SPEC OPS group, who are there to help people. Currently at 7 dollars, this is a game worth looking at....

Pros

- Back to Raccoon City. A fan favorite city
- Co-op is fresh. Feels similar to RE Outbreak
- Controllers are good. You can play with a controller if needed
- Easy to join other players game.
- Can use an Xbox live account if you have one
- Story is alright. About maybe 5 hours of the story (if you take your time). Professional is hard. Everything to unlock everything i would say about 20 hours.
- Graphics are great since this game came out in 2012.

Cons
- AI can be improved. Slow to respond to actions
- Patches are needed to smooth the game (yes, i know. this is not going to happen)
- Multiplayer is pretty much dead
- No real consequences of your actions
- You must create or use your own Xbox live account to save progress. I did find this annoying.
- No Steam achievements...

Overall, pretty solid game. If you want a good shooter that takes place in a zombie filled city, then, why not? Grab a friend and hop on!

Ok, let me be brutally honest for a moment: Operation Raccoon City is an aweful game, but only if you are comparing it to the rest of the Resident Evil Series.

Now let me be brutally honest again: About fifty percent of people who are down rating this are probably looking at this game the wrong way, but by no fault of their own. I already know I'm going to get people hating this reveiw because of this opinion, but hear me out.

Operation Raccoon City is a fun third person shooter. I have only revently gotten into the Resident Evil series. Because of this, I have little to no nostolgia connected to the series. However, after playing about an hour of every Resident Evil game so far, I can completely understand hardcore fan's dislike of the infamous Operation Racoon City. It is nothing like the rest of the series, not even like it's more action based installments such as 6 or the Revelations games.

However, Operation Raccoon City is a good game in its own right. Obviously it has its list of problems, such as its...interesting AI (not nearly as bad as people would have you think, but not great), windows live (not that hard to set up, but just feels really old fashioned), oddly placed difficulty spikes (essentially any level featuring lickers or hunters is unnessisarily difficult to finish), and obvious lack of effort into correctly porting the game onto the pc (navagating the menus is a nightmare, some key rebinding is probably advised, and using a controller will cause you to get a really annoying clicking sound every time you try to go right. This last little gem is because the d-pad on the controller is used for items, and clicking right on the d-pad is used to switch the type of grenade you are using, and for some reason the game gets confused when you go right with the joystick and will not only make your character go right, but will give you the "switched grenade" audio que. No f*cking clue how that even happens.).

But, if you can get past these issues (all of these problems can be solved easily, save for the inclusion of my arch nemesis, hunters), the game has its strong suits too. Gunplay is solid, and weapons actually feel like you are doing damage (the only useless weapon being the pistol, which seems to have the firepower of a small child throwing nerf darts), character design is pretty badass, dialogue is ok, level design is pretty interesting, gameplay is genuinly entertaining, and while the story is essentially an excuse to fit as many recognizable charcters into the game as possible, it certainly makes more sense than some of the other Resident Evil games

If you can play the game with the preverbial grain of salt, there is a lot of enjoyment to be had in this rather underloved installment.

I'm sort of split on this game. In the end I really like it and I had a lot of fun with it on pc and ps3. I dropped a ton of hours into it on ps3 and decided to get the pc version with my friends so we can all play since they didn't have a ps3. The main problem with this game game is that it's a lot of fun with friends, but single player is really lacking. I'm going to strip the Resident Evil tag off this game for a minute and just explore what the game itself contains without a franchise looming over it's expectations.

You choose from six operatives, each with unique abilities. Throughout the game you can purchase new weapons or upgrades for each characters abilities. This adds some replayability but the game itself seems like it was flawed on release. I may seem to be harsh on this game but in the end I will say why I recommend it still, I just feel you should have the full knowledge of what to expect. For my example, I'll just give a run of how a level normally goes.

First off, let's say you want to play online campaign. You will select join game, then after a few minutes you will get thrown into single player since no one plays this game anymore. If you are lucky, you will find a room with just one other person or two. Either way, the level starts, you select a character. The first thing you'll notice is the awkward controls. I highly recommend a controller for this game as the keyboard is very difficult to get used to for this pc port. 

What you may learn also after getting the controls somewhat down is that enemies have switched roles with you. The zombies themselves are easy enough since you can 1 hit kill them with grapples and special attacks, but instead of the player being a bullet sponge and the enemies being made of paper, enemies can take rounds to the face and shrug them off like you were shooting spitballs. Meanwhile one bullet to your body and your health depletes more than half. You can do a 1 hit kill move if you get close enough, but getting that close is near impossible without taking a round to the face and dying. This is definately a game where you have to learn to take things slow. It can get fustrating for new players or people used to a more fast paced action experience. I guess you could consider it somewhat tactical, but simple cover based shooting is hardly a comparison to true tactics. I don't mind the challenge too much but that's just me. 

As for bugs, they exist and you may encounter them. They aren't as frequent as a Bethesda game, but they happen. One time a boss was supposed to appear but never did, forcing me to quit the level. Another time I was supposed to activate a garage door to open it, but the prompt never showed up so we all had to quit on that as well. It's not horrible, as I said they happen rarely, but it's still something that shouldn't of been overlooked in development.

Speaking of development, this game is unfinished. There is a character named Spectre you can play as. At one point in the story line, you have the ability to activate a computer to shut down all generators. He is the only character capable of doing this (it's not very useful since you can just shoot the generators) but this implies that Capcom had intentions of having certain character only interactions with the environment throughout certain levels. No other option exists in the game for any character so it was obviously cut from the game. This kinda sucks as it makes characters less unique. On a side note, if you get the expansion dlc levels where you play as the BSA team, this idea is implemented. So Capcom did probably have intentions to have this in the base game but cut it.

Graphics wise, its ok. For me it works fine but I know my friends had a hard time running this game. The optimization isn't the best so for lower end computers it can get very sluggish. Sound wise the game is fine as well. Guns make gun noises, zombies moan, your character makes sounds when shot; the usual. Nothing exceptionally fancy. 

So far it may seem I've been bashing the game. But there is some things I like. For one, the characters are cool. Their whole persona is let's work together just to get things done. There is no romance, no true friendship, just business. Sadly there personality isn't dipped into much, usually only side comments being made that make their personality, which I feel is appropriate because there not supposed to be the chatty friendly type. Also I'm a sucker for co-op orientated games. If you actually utilize a characters abilities you can pull off some fun gameplay. One of you can go invisible and sneak behind the enemy while one cover fires. You can human shield a zombie, while your teammate throws a sticky bomb onto it, then you throw the zombie into a group of enemies and watch them explode. You can make your own fun somewhat, but as I stated in my first paragraph, this requires human players as A.I. bots don't do any of this. Lastly the gameplay can be interesting. You can human shield an enemy, kick him down to his knees and choose to shoot his head or shoot his stomache to cause him to bleed (bleeding makes it so zombies quickly rush to you and attack, useful for distractions), there is an array of weapons to use like rifles, smgs, shotguns, machine guns, and sniper rifles, and finally special abilites. It would take forever to list special abilites in detail but a few worth noting is one character can disguise as the enemy and roam freely behind enemy lines causing havoc. Another can shoot the zombie virus into a non undead enemy and turn him into a zombie. or shoot an infected enemy to control it. One character even has the support role, where she can shoot darts that buffs teammates.

There is a versus mode online where it's pvp, but to be honest, it's horrible. People abuse cheap mechanics and there isn't much to it. The game is mostly about the co-op storyline element, and the pvp was slapped on because every game now days needs some pvp gameplay.

In the end I do recommend this game. I stated early that I took the Resident Evil tag off this game and judged it without that title. If you look at it from that perspective, it's not a horrible game, it's not polished, but its cooperative content can make you have fun with it. If you add the franchse tag back onto it, I think it lets us know Capcom was trying a new idea. It didn't go perfect, but it was a nice idea.  I enjoy the characters, the atmosphere, the challenge, and if you get the DLC, the game is much better since Capcom took there actual time with that. Either way if you can get a group of three friends to get this game on sale with you, it can be a lot of fun regardless if you are into Resident Evil or not. 

tldr, get on sale with three friends. It's not the best game of it's kind but its unique in itself and can offer some fun gameplay if you take advantage of what the game gives you.

[i]The review is written from a single-player perspective.[/i]

[h1]Short version: 45%[/h1]
Slant Six Games tried, but they were not up to the task to create an interesting and compelling third-person shooter with Operation Raccoon City. The classes, weapons, and their unlock system are great, but the stages are boring and the campaign has no real story.

[h1]Long version:[/h1]
Operation Raccoon City has become quite infamous since its release as the worst Resident Evil game ever made. While it is far from the truth, it is also undeniable that ORC has enormous issues.

The first big problem is that the campaign is criminally short: the par time on its seven missions is barely three and a half hours (granted, the Echo Six DLCs double its length). It has to rely on an unlock system for replay value, where you can grind XP to buy dozens of weapons and skills for each individual character class. This system is common in shooters, but few of them have ORC’s balance. Every class brings a unique set of special skills (although only a handful of them are useful in single-player), and the weapons—except for some infamous DLC additions—cater to many play styles.

Still, good mechanics mean nothing when the level design boils down to copying the same room repeatedly on each stage. Combat is even worse: when we are not fending off the same zombie horde, we participate in generic third-person cover-based shooting against even more generic human soldiers.
Not even the story tries to justify our endless quest for the next set of chest-high walls, because apart from the mission briefing and debriefing screens, there is no plot. The original selling point, promising us the chance to hunt down some famous RE characters thanks to ORC’s non-canon status, is a lie as well. All we get is a 30-second encounter and one large shootout at the very end. Not only it feels like being cheated, but it also shows how lazy the writing got, also reflecting ORC's overall quality.

A perfect love letter for Resident Evil (the ones set in Raccon City) fans!!!

I am such a fan, I finished Resident Evil 1-3 like dozens of times, so due to those countless hours sunk into those games I feel I have an authority to judge this curious instalment in RE saga.

First and foremost... THIS IS NOT ANOTHER CANON RESIDENT EVIL GAME! Get it into your thick skulls you crazy purists!

This is a cooperative action game set in the Resident Evil universe. You can say this game is LEFT 4 DEAD: RESIDENT EVIL EDITION as the game is very similar in many core aspect of the gameplay:

- 4-player coop (bots are available and fill in empty slots)

- you progress through map by doing objectives 

- you got 1 main weapon (shotgun, assault rifles, sinper rifles, SMGs, light machine guns) and 1 sidearms (all kinds of pistols)

- you fight zombies and many other special infected 

- if you get down, other players must revive you


Of course it is not a complete 100% L4D copy! There are differences, the only big one being Third Person Perspective opposed to first person perspective in L4D. Some other diferrences that make the game even better then L4D:

- characters in game have different skills and abilities, you gain experience to level up your chatacter

- you can choose a gun when you start the map

- aside from monster enemies, you also fight armed human enemies

- every time you get hit by zombie/monsters there is a chance you will get infected, if you wont cure the infection before your health runs out, you will become a raging zombie that will viciously attack your companions

But like I said before, there are so many main aspects of the game that are in common with L4D, you should treat it as this kind of game and not a typical RE game.

But that dosent mean it cannot be a survival horror!!! Just switch to the hardest difficulty and enjoy a true survival horror where you must use ammunition, gernades and health items wisely if you want to survive.

That is what this game is, and it is briliant. You can feel that people who created this game loved the Resident Evil games. There are so many details, some bigger and some smaller, that are directly showing this love to the original RE. Calling this game a spin-off would be too much as events in this game are completely different when it comes to some important parts. So I would call it an alternative reality in RE canon, where the events of Raccoon City outbreak occur as they did, but the military and Umbrellas private army had bigger roles in this event. 

There are two sides, the BAD, being Umbrella corps, ruthless guns for hire that do the dirty work and cover up Umbrellas involvement in the incident and the GOOD, being special military unit Echo-6, whose mission is to uncover evidence of Umbrellas fault.

During missons you encounter characters from original RE. As the good guys you help Jill and Carlos fight Nemezis or you help Sherry when she gets separated from Claire in the sewers, you also accompany Claire while she is looking for Sherry. As the bad guys you accompany Hunk as he is about to steal T-Virus from doctor Birkin and you escape Umbrella labs being chased by his mutated version. You encounter Nicolai from RE3 and you chase down Ada Wong only to receive later on an order to... assasinate LEON KENNEDY!

So like I said this a perfect love letter to RE games and it should be treated like that, it is not canon, it is a 'what if' version of events. And as huge RE fan I love it and I think creators did a wonderfull job.

There are plenty of guns in the game, and also every member of the team have different abilities that they can use.

There are also many (if not all) iconic monsters from RE 1-3. You have standard zombies, zombie dogs, but also Lurkers and even TYRANT! And of course that is not all. 

Being able to play up to 4 players and cooperatively playing the missions is a great fun, honestly I liked it even more then Left 4 Dead.

But there is bitter taste in all this tastefull cake... the game has horrible performance, no matter how good PC you have it will still run like sh*t most of the times, it is not unplayable but it is certainly a pain to play very often. The controls are also not very good when it comes to PC standards so many people can have issue with that but I, myself got used to them and they didnt bother me very much after some time.

If only Capcom had invested into getting the game more optimized and removed the GFWL service and replaced it with Steamworks, it would be a perfect game. So sad that they abandoned this game cause it could've been a great game and I would look so much forward to a sequel set in the newer RE games' universe.

It's a pretty generic third person shooter (although I'll admit there are some nice features such as the blood rage stuff (which basically means you could cause severe blood loss from an individual which will attract zombies) and the fact that both human enemies and allies can be bitten and become infected, and there is also a decent amount of enemy variety and classes and special abilities to choose from), which bares the Resident Evil title and is based in the Resident Evil universe. 

Additionally, it's not scary (which isn't suprising considering it's a TPS that gives you loads of weapons and ammo), but there were moments that made me jump enough or had enemies catch me by suprise to make me feel (slightly) on edge and as if I was actually heading through this zombie infested city. 

I'm having some fun with it so far, hence the positive review, but it really isn't amazing. It's not worth full price, however. If you're a Resident Evil fan or just want another basic TPS to play I'd recommend giving it a go. But don't pay full price.

EDIT: At the end of the game there's a two choices than can be made, which I won't mention for spoiler reasons, and they both have decent cutscenes to follow, but the lead into the parts after that choice are insanely hollow. There are no cutscenes after that choice and it practically just throws you straight into that decision without any drama at all. Of course I didn't want it to be insanely over the top dramatic, but having literrally no dramatic introduction to that scene made it feel empty and pointless. Additionally, the only consequences of that decision are a (slightly) different ending boss fight and a different ending cutscene. It's a linear shooter so I'm not suprised, but it feels rather pointless.

That being said I did enjoy the game enough to give it a postive rating and I'm just going through the DLC Echo Six story now. I've not tried the multiplayer as I don't want to and I'd be suprised if anyone still played it.

Unfortunately, the Echo Six story leaves the story with an unresolved cliffhanger, but it's not too annoying. The game is written well enough to be interesting for people who are well into the RE games and for those that are new to them, with gameplay that's challenging enough on normal to be fun.
The game's place in the RE universe isn't strictly canonical/non-canonical, being a ~70% canon "what if?" scenario that is believable enough for the people that know the background material.

That said, it isn't a long game campaign wise, and some of the settings involved are a pain (Games For Windows Live being the top of that list), and is better suited to co-op play with friends than going it alone.

Getting it to work first try just doesn't happen - you have to program remove all Games For Windows Live stuff already on your computer, then reinstall it from the xbox webiste, then reinstall it through the game, then sign in...
...but once you've done that, it just works.

It's probably going to be more enjoyed by the kind of people that liked the Left for Dead games, in that its level progression is more forgiving while also having a better range of easier-harder difficulty settings (they feel pretty good for what they're labelled as), access to an extended arsenal that everybody can use but has to be unlocked (without the to-range guns being "stupid strong" - there are a few direct upgrades, but those are only minor, with the big changes also drastically affecting reload time, range etc in a negative trade-offf), and abilities.

The grenades system is familiar enough for those players, but the special grenades and one-use items are improved on - there are two characters for every class (one for one campaign, one for the other), and each of those gets two passive abilities that can be upgraded and chooses one from three active abilities that can be upgraded, resulting in easy to select varying gameplay per person and a largely range of 'special items', which can be used multiple times due to the recharge mechanic.

The health system is also better. There's the normal healing items that you can carry, which also heal any allies you're next to, and a virus mechanic that can turn your downed allies into an enemy (don't worry, even if you blow their legs off, you can still revive them good as new - and they get their base kit back!), and you can heal that or go on the run for a while if you don't have access to the right tools, but two classes are also set for dealing with it.
The big thing though is that you can just... revive people. You don't have prone time, but you don't need it, as you just get them back up ready to go pretty easily.

6.5-7/10 game for objectively, though it'll obviously score less with people that were never going to like the game.

I got Resident Evil Operation Raccoon City the other day when it was on sale and played it for the first time. Despite the low ratings, I found it a lot of fun. I played single player and co-op and both are great, but I like co-op better. I'm not a fan of the Resident Evil games, but since this one was made as an action shooter, I like it much better. I haven't had any problems with the game except for, when I tried loading the game for the second time after taking a break, it would crash and not load. I'm running windows 8 and found a fix on Youtube.

Operation Raccoon City. "The Ugly Duckling" in Resident Evil franchise. The precusor of the changes that the Resident Evil franchise has experienced. Changes that shook the RE fanbase at it's very foundations. Changes that haunt people to this day. Changes that made people who accepted them to be shunned and called heretics or even worse - casuals.
   
No more classical steady aim, its run and shoot now. Dodge and and squeeze the trigger and let god sort em' out. This is the game that set new directions and gameplay changes that were the backbone of Revelations and RE6 gameplay mechanics. 

No more "jumpscare-conserve-your-ammo" scary, instead it's "get-into-cover-and watch-to-not-get-owerwhelmed-by-whatever-the-game-throws-at-you-while-you-keep-throwing-grenades-and-blindfire-like-crazy" scary. And dodge. Always dodge. Especially when Fighting against T-103's and MA-124's. 
Of course there are some jumpscares still but if you played Resident Evil before they are as predictable as they always were. 

If you're an RE fan - remeber how you used to go back time and time again, either to fix some random tram wire, use a key or get that morgue door open to get the gun? Forget it, there is no going back this time. There's no puzzles either. The only puzzle you'll ever have is trying to understand and cope with the teammates AI - especially if you'll try to play offline. When the AI teammates are just your group filler it's slightly better - but only at a statistical margin of error. I guess they do their best to keep it real and die as often as possible to enhance your feeling of hoplesness and despair just to keep up the biohazard zombie horror appocalypse theme. 

Playing with real people, now this is where the fun begins. If you get a well oriented people that know the ropes, feel and fill their roles, you can have almost an action movie experience - the one the subpar movies have never gave you. Otherwise you can feel like a one man hero, real wolfpack leader, trying to save the day. Or at least try to and fail miserably and be ensured that this is just a nice zombie fairy tale and in real life it's impossible to survive it without teamwork and dealing with other peoples selfishnes. (You bastards picking up first aid kids when I'm a medic and I can heal you better with them than you can heal yourself - I'm pointing at you)  

And don't trust your teammates too much, in the end you will find out that they might not feel the same about what you've all went through.


Despite recieving many negative reviews both from the players and the press this game is not as bad as it seems so don't believe everything you've read or heard. Personally I believe that this is one of the most underappreciated games of these few last years. When it comes to Resident Evil franchise, sure, it falls out of canon - in terms of gameplay - but it does that well in order to be what it is. 

When it comes to storyline it's non-canon too, a hypothethical scenario, but the way it's presented, the mix of real protagonists and antagonists, revisiting places from RE2 and RE3 can make you feel like it's the story untold. The story about desperate attempt to cover up the greatest viral outbreak in the whole Resident Evil franchise, something that a company like Umbrella - with its both private and goverment funding and with it's own special forces and R&D divisions - would most likely attempt to cover up. And thats where you step in as the cover up team alongside your favourite Umbrella Security Service cleaner HUNK (guest appearance in RE2 cinematics, many RE games extra modes and first mision in ORC)
There's also the DLC that allows you to play the gov side that tries to investigate the outbreak on their own and assess the situation - I've found those missions are tougher and more challenging, but its good to see both sides of the story.
  
This game was meant to be a step into another direction, away from mainstream series and it did it well. Imagine an Left4Dead game with third person perspective and an Resident Evil theme - thats Operation Raccoon City. Does it have replayability value? That depends. If you like to play better and better the same scenarios with diffrent random people - just like in L4D - then sure, it has great replayability value. If you want to just do a co-op with random players once in a while - sure it does. You want some sense of achievement? Sure there are guns and skills to unlock. (really usefull once you learn the misions scenarios and figure will you need a cqc or something with more kick, if you are forced to play with one class or another cause others pick it first). It will get extremly repetetive at some point though, but if you are a RE fan and you love Raccoon City as the best RE setting - you will enjoy coming back, even if its just once in a blue moon.

The classical games of the Resident Evil franchise are mostly about surviving, dealing with the tension of managing low supplies and also some puzzle solving. Well, you can basically say goodbye to all of those features in this game, because it's basically an action-oriented title which surely does a great job at it. Now that the basic mechanics were explained, what about the story? There're two different storylines to be mentioned: In the first one, you control a bunch of mercs who're there trying to erase all the data related to the Umbrella's incident, in other words, you take the role of the bad guys. As for the other one, it's the other way around, I mean, you lead a team that is there looking for survivors. The graphics are cool, the soundtrack is ok too, there's nothing exceptional to be mentioned besides that though. As for the gameplay itself, I really don't advise playing the game on your own, because the AI is so dumb that your teammates all behave like a bunch of pigeons. Besides that, you may also bump into one or two glitches that can be really annoying (especially the elevator one), although in my personal opinion they aren't enough bad to spoil the whole experience. There're several different characters that you can choose and each of them have special skills and weapons, which can be unlocked through experience points and that is something cool. I can't really say anything concerning compatibility problems because I still use Win7. Either way, me and my friends had to deal with a headache while we were trying to play online but fortunately that problem was solved after some ports were opened at the router.

Tl;dr - Forget about the classical Resident Evil games. This is basically Gears of War with zombies and it's definitely meant to be played with your friends, not alone.

Steam asked if I wanted to update my review, so here goes.  I was especially salty when I wrote my original review because this is a game I was very hype to play.  I was extremely disappointed by it.

The game still uses Games For Windows Live, so you will need to follow a community guide and do some tinkering.  On top of that, if you are actually going to attempt to play this, make sure you have both of the windows 10 Xbox apps open and signed in: the built in companion app, and the newer downloadable one.  Having to do all this just to get the game to function is strike one.

I played the game through again with two of my friends, and the honest truth is that while the game has its moments, it is horribly unbalanced and if you don't have 2 or more actual human beings it becomes frustratingly hard even on the easiest difficulty.  The game really needs to go easier on you when you are not playing with 4 human beings, the teammate Ai is abysmally bad while the enemy Ai seems to have literal aimbot at times.  I tried playing the game by myself on PS3 years ago and literally couldn't bring myself to do it because my Ai companions would die very quickly, leaving me to fend for myself with very limited ammo and only one ability that has a long cooldown (and also may or may not actually do anything useful if you're playing alone, depending on what character you play as).  Strike two.

There are a lot of great ideas here, they are just not executed very well.  I also believe that the game should have focused on creating an interesting behind-the-scenes of Resident Evil 2, it has the potential to do that and I think that would have been really cool.  Instead, it's a non-canon what-if game.  So, not only is the gameplay a mess, but the story is completely irrelevant to the story/lore of rest of the games that Resident Evil/Biohazard fans care about, or even the movies which would at least be something.  What is the motivation to suffer through this unpolished, unbalanced, unpatched product?  Three strikes, you're out.

I'll give the game brownie points because it did make my friends and I laugh quite a few times at how bad it was.  Also, there were also a couple of cool story and gameplay moments; the cast of the main campaign is interesting and I enjoyed listening to the unique conversations that would play depending on which of the 4 characters were in your squad.  You can tell there were people on the development team who cared about what they were making.  I respect that and I feel bad that their project flopped so hard.  Plus, it's Raccoon City.  That was a huge selling point and built hype; aside from the on-the-rail shooter side games, Raccoon City's iconic locations hadn't really been given a true "HD" treatment until this installment.  They are neat to walk through even if a lot of the areas don't stay faithful to their original layouts.  Sadly, good art can't save a bad game.

Zombies will not reliably attack you unless you are bleeding, which is a good game mechanic for multiplayer, but even when you are bleeding they often ignore you and the same applies to enemies. Hunters will literally run up to you, and troll you.

All of the B.O.W.s work on aggro, so, whoever shoots the Tyrants more, that's who it goes after. Some of the actives in this game, much more so than the passives, are complete broken ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. RPG abilities do not belong in shooters, ever, and this is no exception. This game does have many good game modes, like G-Virus sample mode, which is essentially capture the G-virus (like CTF). All of the game modes, minus Heroes, are fun, they are just crippled by broken weapons. There can be good and bad said about this, but overall, I love it.

   First of all, this game is extremely underrated. 
On the one hand, it's short, being able to finish the entire base campaign in about 4 hours if you know what you're doing, blowing through enemies, but still grabbing collectibles along the way (they are required for your chapter rankings in this one.) For example, look at my hours played (7.3 at the time of this review) - I've played all the way through the main campaign twice in just over 7 hours... Also, you have no ability to order your team where to go, which could come in handy if you want to do a mass team heal with one First Aid Spray, and once in a blue moon, the game will glitch in a way that prevents you from continuing, and the only way to fix it is to return to the main menu and reload... or die. This game could have really used a "Restart Last Checkpoint" option. This can be pretty brutal during the Echo Six DLC, because is not started the same way as the base campaign and you cannot return to a checkpoint if you return to the Main Menu, only if you die. And no, it is pretty much impossible to kill yourself if there are no enemies present at the time of the glitch. Also your squad would probably kill them anyway. Speaking of the AI though, they do die a lot. Sometimes you just have to pick your battles and make it to the next checkpoint to get them back instead of going back and reviving them manually.
   
On the other hand, it's an amazing game to play with a few friends, and for being a few years old and having a bad overall reception, this game has a rather large cult following, and it actually still isn't too hard to play online.  As short as it is, fans of it have no problem playing through the campaign over and over, with diferent character/ability/weapon combos without it ever getting old. 
All in all, if you find that you enjoy this game, it's replay value soars sky-high. This is great, because if it had no replay value and a 4 hour campaign, this definitely would not be a positive review.
Should you decide to pick this one up, definitely get the complete pack. The Echo Six DLC is literally half the game. It has increased difficulty over the main campaign and basically raises the play time of the whole thing to 8-9 hours if you don't have to restart checkpoints, for the feeling of a more complete gaming experience.

Resident Evil ORC Review:

Resident Evil Operation Racoon City is lame, a let down, and a pain in your rear end.

The game takes place in Racoon City during the Infamous infection time, (Same time as Resident Evil 2 & 3). You are part of a squad from Umbrella that must follow orders and do missions within the disastrous and unstable Raccoon City. 

You are a squadron of 4 deployed by Umbrella, you get to choose your character you play as, aswell as the companions you bring along with you, note the campaign can also be played with 4 other players to have a full coop story experience.

There is a a few different classes and characters, such as Vector(Recon), Lupo, Beltway (Explosive Specialist), Spectre (Marksman), Bertha (Medic), FourEyes (Scientist). They all have different abilities such as Stealth, Seeing through Walls, Plantings explosives, Healing, & all kinds of different perks. Which is nice to be able to choose whom you enjoy playing as the most.

You can unlock new weapons, perks & abilities by buying them with XP which is nice. Though the level system is quite redundent.

The story itself is mediocre, nothing to shabby or to keep you wanting to move forward, you end up just shugging along although it was nice to see characters such as Nemesis, Leon, Claire, Sherry & Ada during your travels in Raccoon City. It was a nice cross-over with Resident Evil 2-3's story although this games story is Non-Canon to the series.

Now well the big part, the Gameplay. I found this game to be entertaining most times. Shooting up zombies and infected, (those Crimson Heads & Hunters sure could be a pain) but I enjoyed having a challenge with B.O.W's which was nice and shooting up zombies on the streets of Raccoon City.
 
What I absolutely despised about this game was the "Enemy Soldiers", they were literarly your worst nightmare and they were freaking everywhere you go in this damn game. They would be spammed in large numbers and were hard to kill, they would Harass/Aim-Bot/Shoot You Up as if you were trying to land on D-Day. One soldier could literarly murder you within 2 seconds if your not in cover, now imagine 15 of them clumped like a bunker you have to get through (Dying Simulater begins). The Enemy Soldier A.I are ridiculously hard in this game even on Normal and they will kill you.

Remember when I mentioned getting through soldiers is like attempting to get through a bunker with an automated turret?, well imagine that but with 20 zombies harassing you at the same time, is that not enough how about annoying Crimson Heads and Hunters, yea your gonna get real angry during situations like that because this game is stupidly unbalanced.

Ah, so you cleared the area of Zombies & B.O.W's?, well you better watch out because that soldier over there just killed  you. Oh?, not a problem right this game has checkpoints?, Oh did I forget to mention this game has one of the worst Checkpoints systems I have ever seen... If you clear a room of 50 people proceed a bit further and die... well guess what? you gotta clear all that bull crap again, and it will happen ALOT in this game.

But, I have A.I Partners to help me right?, Your A.I Partners are useless as Nipples on a Man. They may get a few zombie kills, but oh boy when it comes to fighting Soldiers & B.O.W's you are the one whos gonna do all the work. Example of treachery: You have Bertha on your team because she's a medic, well she aint gonna heal you when you absolutely need it, you could be right next to her with little to no health and she will prioretize any enemy over healing your behind.

If you got friends you can play with, do it because the A.I are useless, YOU are the one man army here with a bunch of monkeys with guns.

This game has a crappy Auto-Cover system, more reason to die.

Overall, this game can provide entertainment. I had fun playing it, apart from the deaths from soldiers of course. Is it worth its retail value?, Absolutely not BUY IT ON SALE as I did, no more than $10 should you pay for this game.

FOR THOSE OF YOU WHO CAN'T LAUNCH THE GAME:

- Open your start menu and search for 'Uninstall a program'.
- Uninstall 'Microsoft Games for Windows - Live Redistributable'.
- Uninstall 'Microsoft Games for Windows Marketplace'.
- Download and install GFWL from -  https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=201134  (Credit to Steam User 'Arkais' for finding the link)

With that out of the way, is this game actually worth $29.99? Simple answer - no.

Operation Raccoon City forces you to play alongside three other members in your squad for the entire game. This isn't a problem if you have three friends to play with, but considering how unpopular this game is, chances are you'll be playing with at least one bot, and you won't be able to fathom how mind-blowingly stupid they can be. They stare at walls during battle, stand in front of gunfire, run into crowds of zombies and spray you down with first-aid when you have so much as a paper cut. Occasionally they'll shoot at the enemy to little effect.

Awful AI aside, the game is rife with bugs, clunky controlling and horrible gameplay mechanics.

If you're adamant on buying this, wait for a Steam sale.

First Impression (Will change when game is done)

So far, I'm not seeing why this game got such immense hate. Sure it isn't the best game in the world, and it doesn't encapture that old Resident Evil feel, but let's be real for a minute. Fans of the series who kept on hoping that Resident Evil would re-encapture the horror of the original 3 are going to be sorely dissappointed. The series moved into a more action oriented genre with 4, becoming more action-oriented with each iteration after 4. So the fact that people are acting surprised that ORC was primarily action based need to get a reality check. Comparing this to any other Resident Evil will basically give you the worst impression of all. This was meant to be a completely stand alone title, giving a non-canon hypothetical scenario that takes place between 2 and 3, where you play as the bad guys basically.

As for the game itself, aside from the terrible friendly AI and GFWL, ORC has some good gameplay to be had. A linear shooter, where it becomes cover-based against humans, and turns into an all out slaughterhouse against zombies, it flips between the two surprisingly well. The story is pretty cheesy and feels a bit half-ass, but again most of Resident Evil's story telling is not all that exceptional. They all feel like a cheap B movie became a longer than expected series, but never got past its B movie storytelling. But I do cherish that in Resident Evil and can enjoy the stupidity and silliness. 

I wouldn't reccommend this game at full price right now, but it is definately worth 10 bucks, especially if you have someone to play with and can deal with GFWL.

I can't really call myself a true Resident Evil fan, I've only recently managed to play Resident Evil 4 and have never played any of the original games (I.E Resident Evil 1-3). I will go ahead now and say I rather enjoy this game quite a bit, it's certainly got enough charm for a quick game every now and then but it doesn't have the lasting draw that most other RE games have. Resident Evil: Operation Raccoon City did some things right, but did quite a lot at a mediocre level and some things plain badly, so I'll tell you what i think, and you can decide for yourself.

The Good 
-The Character design: The characters and most enemies in this game are quite varied in appearance and personality, and I like that. Mainly I'm talking about Wolf Pack here, they each have an interesting back-story that is never mentioned in-game (you'll need an external source like a wikia for that) and they all look unique and interesting. Personally if they were a little more developed I wouldn't mind seeing them in other games.
-The Music: I'll say now regardless of how one-sided my opinion is, I love the music in the game. It's a mix of atmospheric tones to intense dramatic symphonies, all of them fit their respective situations perfectly.

The Okay
-The Cover mechanics: Cover in this game is a bit iffy, some things you can hide behind others you can't sometimes you can shoot from cover sometimes you can't. It's kinda like rolling the dice with your health and that's never a good thing.
-The Combat mechanics: Combat is arguably the main aspect of RE:ORC, and when the main aspect of the game isn't the best part of the game, you're not in for a good time. Recoil feels almost non-existent but bullet spread is a pain to manage, especially with the less accurate weapons. The meele combat is okay, however performing executions and special moves is unresponsive and it usually takes multiple attempts to perform one.

The Bad
- Enemy design : Enemies in this game can be easily described with the term "bullet sponge". They all take a hell of a lot of ammo to kill and that's not helping the face you hardly have any to begin with. This isn't a problem when it comes to the slow and easy to deal with zombies, but when faced with enemy humans, hunters and lickers it becomes a huge problem and is even more apparent in the harder difficulties. Additionally shooting enemies hardly causes them to react, they just take it like nothing has happened most of the time which is frustrating when it comes to already hard to kill enemies like the hunters or the final boss depending on what choice you make.
- The Story: Not much to say here, even for a spin off title in an alternate reality the story of this game is really weak and boring with no real development of characters.

All in all, RE:ORC is a game that's fun with friends, but not worth the given price-tag. Give it a shot if you can ever get it cheaper but don't expect to be amazed by the game.
